merge-pdf.name: Merge PDF
merge-pdf.desc: Combine multiple PDF files into one, drag and drop to set the order, rotate files as needed.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste (Ctrl/⌘ + V) the PDF files to merge.
Drag and drop or use the ↑ ↓ buttons to set the order; click ↻ to rotate a file that's upside down.
Click “Merge PDF” and download the result, or pass it on to another tool.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Merging runs entirely in JavaScript in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Can I merge password-protected PDFs?
faq.a: Yes, if you know the password. You'll be asked for it when opening the file, and the result has no password.

faq.q: Is there a limit on files or size?
faq.a: No fixed limit; the practical limit is your device's memory. On phones, keep each merge under about 200 MB.

split-pdf.name: Split PDF
split-pdf.desc: Split a PDF by page ranges, one file per page, or extract the pages you pick.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste (Ctrl/⌘ + V) the PDF to split.
Choose how to split: by page ranges (e.g. 1-3, 4-8), every N pages, or click the pages to extract.
Click “Split PDF” and download each file or all of them as a .zip.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: How do I split every page into its own file?
faq.a: Choose “Every N pages” with N = 1, or choose “Pick pages”, select the pages and turn on “Each selected page becomes its own file”.

faq.q: Does splitting reduce quality?
faq.a: No. Pages are copied intact into the new files: text stays selectable and images keep their sharpness.

faq.q: What about password-protected files?
faq.a: Enter the password when asked; the split files won't have a password.

remove-pages-pdf.name: Delete PDF Pages
remove-pages-pdf.desc: Click the pages you don't need and remove them from the PDF.
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF file.
Click the pages to remove (hold Shift to select a range) or type page numbers, e.g. 2, 5-7.
Click “Delete pages” and download the new file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Is the original file changed?
faq.a: No. The tool creates a new PDF without the selected pages; the original on your device stays the same.

faq.q: I want to keep a few pages rather than delete many?
faq.a: Use Split PDF in “Pick pages” mode to extract exactly the pages you want to keep.

organize-pdf.name: Organize PDF Pages
organize-pdf.desc: Drag and drop to reorder pages, rotate, delete, insert blank pages or other PDFs.
howto: Choose one or more PDF files; the pages of every file appear in a grid.
Drag and drop pages (or use the ← → buttons) to reorder; rotate ↺ ↻, delete 🗑 or add blank pages as needed.
Click “Save PDF” to download the file with the new page order.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Does drag and drop work on phones?
faq.a: On phones, use the ← → buttons under each page to move it; the rotate and delete buttons are always visible.

faq.q: Can I insert pages from another file in the middle?
faq.a: Yes. Click “Add PDF” to add a file; its pages appear at the end, then drag them where you need.

faq.q: What are blank pages for?
faq.a: Usually for double-sided printing, so a new chapter starts on an odd page, or to leave room for notes.

rotate-pdf.name: Rotate PDF
rotate-pdf.desc: Rotate individual pages or the whole PDF to the right reading orientation.
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF file.
Click an upside-down page to rotate it 90° (↺ ↻ to rotate left/right), or rotate all pages at once.
Click “Rotate PDF” and download the rotated file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Does rotating blur text or images?
faq.a: No. The tool only changes the page's display orientation in the file; content keeps its quality.

faq.q: Can I rotate just a few pages?
faq.a: Yes. Click exactly the pages to rotate; the others stay as they are.

compress-pdf.name: Compress PDF
compress-pdf.desc: Reduce PDF size for email and messaging while text stays sharp and selectable.
howto: Choose or drag and drop one or more PDF files.
Choose a compression level: light, recommended or strong.
Click “Compress PDF”, see how much smaller it got, then download.

faq.q: Does compressing blur the text?
faq.a: No. The tool only recompresses the images inside the file; text and vector graphics stay untouched, so they remain sharp and selectable.

faq.q: Why did my file shrink so little?
faq.a: Mostly-text PDFs are already compact. The tool helps most with scanned PDFs or ones with many photos.

faq.q: Is the file sent to a server for compression?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in your browser.

pdf-to-image.name: PDF to Image
pdf-to-image.desc: Convert each PDF page into a high-quality JPG or PNG image.
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF file.
Choose JPG or PNG and the resolution (DPI); deselect pages you don't need.
Click “Convert to images” and download each image or all of them as a .zip.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Should I choose JPG or PNG?
faq.a: JPG is light, good for messaging and email. PNG is sharpest for pages with small text or tables, but the files are larger.

faq.q: What is DPI and what should I pick?
faq.a: DPI is the number of pixels per inch of paper. 150 DPI is enough for screens; 300 DPI for printing. Higher DPI means sharper and larger images.

faq.q: Can I convert hundreds of pages?
faq.a: Yes, pages are converted one by one. On phones, choose a lower DPI to run faster and use less memory.

image-to-pdf.name: Image to PDF
image-to-pdf.desc: Combine JPG, PNG images and screenshots into a single PDF file.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste (Ctrl/⌘ + V) images: JPG, PNG, HEIC, screenshots…
Order the pages by dragging or with ↑↓, rotate upside-down images; choose paper size, orientation, margins and quality.
Click “Convert to PDF” and download the file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Do iPhone photos (HEIC) work?
faq.a: Yes. The tool reads HEIC images and rotates them correctly based on the image's orientation info.

faq.q: How do I make the PDF smaller?
faq.a: Choose “Light” quality. If it's still large, run it through Compress PDF.

faq.q: Can each image become its own PDF?
faq.a: Yes, turn off “Combine all images into one PDF”; download the files one by one or together in a .zip.

pdf-to-text.name: PDF to Text
pdf-to-text.desc: Extract all the text from a PDF to copy or save as a .txt file.
howto: Choose or drag and drop one or more PDF files.
Choose whether to show page numbers and whether to join lines broken mid-sentence.
Click “Extract text”, view it right away, copy it all or download a .txt file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Why can't I get text from my file?
faq.a: Scanned PDFs (photographed or scanned from paper) only contain images, with no text layer. Use Image to Text (OCR).

faq.q: Do accented characters show correctly in the .txt file?
faq.a: Yes. The file is saved as UTF-8 with a BOM, so Notepad and Word read it correctly.

faq.q: Are tables and formatting kept?
faq.a: No. The tool only extracts plain text; tables become lines of text.

sign-pdf.name: Sign PDF
sign-pdf.desc: Draw, type or upload your signature; add text and dates to PDF pages.
howto: Choose or drag and drop the PDF to sign.
Click “Create a new signature”: draw it, type your name or choose a photo of your signature; you can also add text, dates, check marks and stamp images.
Drag the signature into place, drag a corner to resize, then click “Sign and download”.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Is this a digital signature?
faq.a: No. It's an image signature (like signing by hand and scanning), fine for everyday contracts and forms. Digital signatures use certificates issued by a provider and need special software.

faq.q: Where is my signature stored?
faq.a: Created signatures are only saved in this device's browser for reuse. Click × on a signature to delete it.

faq.q: Can I sign several pages at once?
faq.a: Yes. Select the signature on the page and click “Copy to every page”.

page-numbers-pdf.name: Add Page Numbers to PDF
page-numbers-pdf.desc: Add page numbers at the top or bottom of pages, choosing the position and style.
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF file.
Choose the position, number style (1, Page 1, 1 / 10…), and whether to skip the cover; see the preview on the pages.
Click “Page numbers” and download the file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: If I skip the cover, where does numbering start?
faq.a: The cover has no number and the second page gets the starting number (1 by default). You can change the starting number under “More options”.

faq.q: Are landscape (rotated) pages numbered in the right spot?
faq.a: Yes. The number's position follows the page orientation as you see it.

watermark-pdf.name: Watermark PDF
watermark-pdf.desc: Stamp semi-transparent text or a logo onto PDF pages.
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF file.
Type text or choose a logo; adjust opacity, angle, position, or tile it across the page.
Preview it on the pages, click “Add watermark” and download the file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Can the watermark be removed?
faq.a: The watermark is drawn into the page content. Choose “Tile across the page” to make it harder to crop out.

faq.q: Can I use a logo with a transparent background?
faq.a: Yes. Use a PNG with a transparent background for the best look on any page background.

faq.q: Can I watermark only some pages?
faq.a: Yes. Choose “Some pages” and enter, e.g., 1-3, 5.

protect-pdf.name: Protect PDF with Password
protect-pdf.desc: Lock a PDF with a password using AES-256 encryption.
howto: Choose or drag and drop one or more PDF files.
Enter the password twice; if needed, open “Restrict permissions” to block printing, copying or editing.
Click “Lock PDF” and download the encrypted file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Is the encryption secure?
faq.a: Files are encrypted with AES-256 per the PDF 2.0 standard. The longer and less guessable the password, the safer.

faq.q: What if I forget the password?
faq.a: It can't be recovered. Keep the password somewhere safe and keep the unlocked original.

faq.q: Are print and copy restrictions guaranteed?
faq.a: Popular PDF readers respect them, but some software may ignore them. The open password is the real protection.

unlock-pdf.name: Unlock PDF
unlock-pdf.desc: Remove the password (when you know it) and print/copy restrictions from a PDF.
howto: Choose or drag and drop one or more PDF files.
For files that need a password to open: click 🔒 and enter it. Files that only restrict printing or copying need nothing.
Click “Unlock PDF” and download the unlocked file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Can it crack a password I forgot?
faq.a: No. The tool only unlocks files when you know the open password. Print/copy restrictions (no password needed to open) are removed right away.

faq.q: Is unlocking legal?
faq.a: Only unlock your own files or files you're allowed to use.

extract-pages-pdf.name: Extract PDF Pages
extract-pages-pdf.desc: Pick the pages you want and save them as a new PDF file.
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF file.
Click the pages to extract (hold Shift to select a range) or type page numbers, e.g. 1, 3-5.
Click “Extract pages” to download the new file; turn on “Each page as a separate file” if needed.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: How is this different from Split PDF?
faq.a: Extract takes exactly the pages you pick into one file. Split PDF divides the whole file into parts by page ranges or every N pages.

faq.q: Is page quality reduced?
faq.a: No. Pages are copied intact: text stays selectable and images keep their sharpness.

extract-images-pdf.name: Extract Images from PDF
extract-images-pdf.desc: Get the original images embedded in a PDF file.
howto: Choose or drag and drop one or more PDF files.
Choose a minimum size to skip icons and thin lines.
Click “Extract images” and download each image or a .zip.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Is image quality reduced?
faq.a: JPEG images are taken as is from the file, without recompression. Other images are saved as lossless PNG, keeping transparency.

faq.q: Why can't I get charts or text?
faq.a: Charts and text are usually vector drawings, not images. Use PDF to Image to capture whole pages.

crop-pdf.name: Crop PDF
crop-pdf.desc: Trim white margins or unwanted areas from PDF pages.
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF file.
Choose “Auto-remove white margins” (optionally keep a few mm, crop all pages evenly) or enter the margins in mm; the blue frame on the page is the part that's kept.
Click “Crop margins” and download the file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Is the cropped area deleted?
faq.a: No. The tool resets the page's visible area (CropBox); content outside is only hidden. Don't rely on cropping to remove sensitive information.

faq.q: What is cropping good for?
faq.a: Bigger text when reading on a phone, printing scans without black borders, or removing extra margins before combining with other documents.

insert-blank-pdf.name: Insert Blank Pages
insert-blank-pdf.desc: Add blank pages anywhere in a PDF, e.g. for double-sided printing.
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF file.
Choose where to insert: after or before selected pages, after every page, at the end, or to make the page count even; click pages to pick positions.
Preview the blank pages in the page grid, click “Insert blank pages” and download the file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: What size are the blank pages?
faq.a: The same size and orientation as the page right before them, so printing lines up.

faq.q: Why make the page count even for double-sided printing?
faq.a: When printing several documents in a row double-sided, an odd page count makes the next document start on the back of the previous one's last sheet. One blank page avoids that.

grayscale-pdf.name: Grayscale PDF
grayscale-pdf.desc: Convert a color PDF to grayscale to save ink, with text still selectable.
howto: Choose or drag and drop one or more PDF files.
Click “Convert to grayscale”.
Download the grayscale file to print without color ink.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Is text turned into images?
faq.a: No. Colors are changed inside the page content, so text stays sharp, selectable and searchable like the original.

faq.q: Why is there still some color?
faq.a: A few rare elements (JPEG 2000 images, special color spaces) can't be converted yet; the tool reports how many after converting.

metadata-pdf.name: Edit PDF Metadata
metadata-pdf.desc: View and edit a PDF's title, author, subject and keywords (metadata).
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF file; its current info is filled in.
Edit the title, author, subject, keywords…, or turn on “Remove all hidden info”.
Click “Save info” and download the file.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: What is PDF metadata for?
faq.a: The title shows in the tab when the file is opened, and helps search and sort documents. The author and creator software may reveal information you don't want to share.

faq.q: Why is the XMP block removed after editing?
faq.a: XMP is an XML copy of the info that some readers prefer; if kept, the old info might still show. The tool removes it so the new info takes effect.

fill-form-pdf.name: Fill PDF Form
fill-form-pdf.desc: Fill in the form fields of a PDF (applications, declarations) and save it.
howto: Choose or drag and drop a PDF that has form fields.
Click the blue boxes on the page to type, check or choose options; press Tab to go to the next field.
Click “Save filled PDF”; turn on “Flatten after filling” if recipients shouldn't be able to edit it.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Will accented characters display correctly?
faq.a: Yes. When needed, the tool embeds the Be Vietnam Pro font into the file so every PDF reader shows the text correctly.

faq.q: What if my file has no fields to fill?
faq.a: Use Sign PDF to add text, dates, check marks or signatures anywhere on the page.

faq.q: Can XFA forms (Adobe LiveCycle) be filled?
faq.a: Only the regular form part (AcroForm) that comes with them. XFA-only forms need Adobe Acrobat.

flatten-pdf.name: Flatten PDF Form
flatten-pdf.desc: Turn filled form fields into fixed content that can no longer be edited.
howto: Choose or drag and drop one or more PDFs with filled forms.
Click “Flatten form”.
Download the file: the filled content is fixed and can no longer be edited.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Does flattening lose the filled content?
faq.a: No. The content stays on the page; only the fields are no longer editable.

faq.q: Can it be undone?
faq.a: Not on the flattened file. Keep the original if you may need to edit it again.

view-pdf.name: PDF Viewer
view-pdf.desc: Open and read PDFs right in your browser, search text, zoom and go full screen.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste a PDF file.
Scroll to read; use the toolbar to jump to pages, zoom in and out or go full screen.
Type in the search box (accents optional) and press Enter for the next match; select text to copy it.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Does searching “cafe” find “café”?
faq.a: Yes. Search ignores letter case and accents.

faq.q: How do I print the file?
faq.a: Click the printer button to open the file in the browser's built-in PDF viewer, then print from there.

faq.q: Can I view password-protected files?
faq.a: Yes, enter the password when asked. It's only used on your device.

scan-document.name: Document Scanner
scan-document.desc: Photograph documents with your camera, auto-straighten, whiten the background and export to PDF.
howto: Click “Open camera” and shoot the paper (on a darker surface, with enough light), or choose existing photos.
Check the 4 automatically detected corners and drag to adjust if needed; choose the Color, Gray or Black & white filter, then click “Add page”.
Capture more pages, reorder them, choose the paper size and click “Create PDF”.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every step runs in JavaScript right in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: Are the photos sent online?
faq.a: No. The camera, the photos, the straightening and background whitening all run on your device.

faq.q: How do I get the best scan?
faq.a: Place the paper on a dark surface, avoid shadows from your hand and phone, shoot straight down and hold steady. Black & white suits text documents; Color suits stamped papers and pictures.

faq.q: What if the paper corners aren't found?
faq.a: Drag the 4 round handles to the 4 corners of the paper, or click “Use the whole image”. On a computer you can nudge each corner with the arrow keys.

compress-image.name: Compress Images
compress-image.desc: Reduce the size of JPG, PNG and WebP images in bulk, with a mode to get below the KB you need.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste (Ctrl/⌘ + V) one or more images.
Choose the quality, or turn on “Compress below” and enter the target size in KB (e.g. 200 KB for online forms).
Click “Compress images”, compare before/after, then download each image or a .zip.

faq.q: Are my images sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Images are compressed right in your browser with MozJPEG/WebP encoders running in WebAssembly.

faq.q: Can I get below 100 KB?
faq.a: Yes. Turn on “Compress below” and enter 100; the tool lowers quality and, if needed, the dimensions until it gets there.

faq.q: Is the GPS location kept in the image?
faq.a: No. Compressed images have no EXIF/GPS data; the orientation is already applied.

resize-image.name: Resize Image
resize-image.desc: Shrink or enlarge images by pixels, percentage or longest side.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste one or more images (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC…).
Choose how to resize: enter pixels (leave one box empty to keep the ratio), a percentage, or the longest side (e.g. 1920 px).
Click “Resize” and download each image or a .zip.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Does shrinking make images jagged?
faq.a: No. Images are downscaled in halving steps with a high-quality filter, so details stay smooth. Enlarging beyond the original makes images blurry, so by default small images aren't enlarged.

faq.q: How do I get an exact size like 800×800?
faq.a: Turn off “Keep aspect ratio” to stretch to the exact pixels, or crop to 1:1 with Crop Image first and then resize so it isn't distorted.

crop-image.name: Crop Image
crop-image.desc: Crop images freely or to 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, 3:4 ratios.
howto: Choose or drag and drop an image.
Choose a ratio (free, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9…), then drag the box and its corners to select the area to keep; or enter exact pixels.
Click “Crop image” and download the cropped image.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Does cropping reduce quality?
faq.a: The kept area keeps its original resolution. JPGs are saved at quality 92, so the difference is barely visible; choose PNG to keep every pixel.

faq.q: Can I use the keyboard?
faq.a: Yes. Click the crop box, then use the arrow keys to move it and Shift + arrows to resize it.

rotate-image.name: Rotate & Flip Image
rotate-image.desc: Rotate images 90°, 180° or mirror-flip them in bulk.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste one or more images.
Click the rotate left/right or flip buttons on each image, or use “Apply to all images”.
Click “Save images” and download each image or a .zip.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Why do phone photos show up sideways on a computer?
faq.a: Phones often only record the orientation in EXIF instead of rotating the pixels; some software ignores it. This tool actually rotates the pixels, so the image displays correctly everywhere.

faq.q: Can I fix a mirrored selfie with backwards text?
faq.a: Yes. Click “Flip horizontal” to mirror the image and the text reads normally.

convert-image.name: Image Converter
convert-image.desc: Convert between JPG, PNG, WebP and AVIF.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste one or more images (JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, HEIC).
Choose the target format and quality; for JPG you can choose a background color for transparent areas.
Click “Convert” and download each image or a .zip.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Which format should I choose?
faq.a: JPG opens everywhere. WebP is about 25–35% lighter than JPG and supports transparency. AVIF is lightest but slower to encode and some older software can't open it. PNG keeps every pixel, good for screenshots and logos.

faq.q: Do animated GIFs keep their animation?
faq.a: No. The tool only takes the first frame of an animated GIF.

heic-to-jpg.name: HEIC to JPG
heic-to-jpg.desc: Convert iPhone HEIC/HEIF photos to JPG or PNG in bulk, right on your device.
howto: Choose or drag and drop .heic / .heif images (you can pick many at once).
Choose JPG or PNG and the quality.
Click “Convert” and download each image or a .zip.

faq.q: What is HEIC?
faq.a: HEIC (HEIF) is the iPhone's default photo format. It's lighter than JPG, but many Windows PCs, web apps and upload forms can't open it.

faq.q: Are photos uploaded to a server for conversion?
faq.a: No. HEIC decoding runs in WebAssembly (libheif) right in your browser.

faq.q: What about Live Photos or burst shots?
faq.a: The tool takes the main image in the HEIC file. The video part of a Live Photo isn't in the .heic file, so it isn't affected.

id-photo.name: ID Photo Maker
id-photo.desc: Make passport and ID photos from a portrait: AI background replacement, framing and a print sheet with multiple photos.
howto: Choose a straight-on, well-lit portrait showing your shoulders.
Wait for the AI to remove the background and find the face (runs on your device; about 8 MB of models the first time), then choose the background color and photo size.
Drag and zoom so the head fits the guide frame, then download the single photo or a print sheet (4×6 in or A4).

faq.q: Is my photo sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. The background-removal AI model is downloaded and runs right in your browser; the photo never leaves your device.

faq.q: How do I print it at a photo shop?
faq.a: Download the 4×6 in (10×15 cm) sheet at 300 dpi and print it like a regular photo, then cut along the faint lines. To print at home, choose A4 and print at exactly 100% size.

faq.q: What background does an ID photo need?
faq.a: Most documents use a white or light background. Check the requirements of where you're applying; US passports and visas need a white background and 2×2 in size.

remove-bg.name: Remove Background
remove-bg.desc: Remove the background from portraits with AI running on your device; export transparent PNG or a colored background.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste one or more photos of people (portraits, product photos with models).
Choose the new background: transparent (PNG), white, another color or a blurred original.
Click “Remove background”, wait for the AI to process on your device, then download.

faq.q: Are photos sent to a server for AI processing?
faq.a: No. The AI model (MODNet) is downloaded to your browser and runs on your device; photos never leave it.

faq.q: Does it work on objects and animals?
faq.a: The tool is trained to cut out people, so it works best on photos with people. Objects and animals may not be cut out perfectly.

faq.q: Why is the first use a bit slow?
faq.a: The first time, the browser downloads about 6.6 MB of AI model; later uses reuse the cached copy and are much faster.

blur-image.name: Blur & Redact Image
blur-image.desc: Blur or black out ID numbers, license plates and faces before sending a photo.
howto: Choose or drag and drop an image.
Drag on the image to outline areas to cover (ID numbers, plates, faces…), or click “Find faces” to let the AI outline them.
Choose a style (blur, pixelate, black out), click “Save covered image” and download.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Should I blur or black out?
faq.a: For text and numbers (IDs, account numbers, plates), black them out: light blurring can sometimes be reversed. Blur or pixelate suits faces and backgrounds.

faq.q: Does the covered image keep the GPS location?
faq.a: No. The image is re-saved, so it has none of the original's EXIF/GPS data.

strip-exif.name: Remove EXIF & GPS Data
strip-exif.desc: View and remove camera info, date/time and GPS location from photos.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste one or more images (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC…).
See which images have a GPS location; click the icon on an image to see its camera, date/time and coordinates.
Choose “Remove all” or “Remove location only”, click “Remove info” and download the cleaned images.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Do phone photos reveal my location?
faq.a: They can. With location enabled for the camera, photos store the GPS coordinates to within a few meters. Some social networks strip this, but sending original files by email, chat apps (as files) or cloud drives keeps it.

faq.q: Does removing EXIF reduce quality?
faq.a: Not for JPG, PNG or WebP: the tool only removes the info from the file, without recompressing. HEIC images are saved as high-quality JPG.

faq.q: Will photos turn sideways afterwards?
faq.a: No, as long as “Keep orientation” is on: the tool keeps the one tag that says whether the photo is portrait or landscape.

watermark-image.name: Watermark Images
watermark-image.desc: Stamp text or a logo onto images in bulk to protect product photos.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste one or more images.
Type text (or choose a logo), adjust size, opacity, angle and position; turn on “Tile across the image” to make it hard to crop out.
Preview on the first image, click “Add watermark” and download each image or a .zip.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Is the watermark consistent on images of different sizes?
faq.a: Yes. Text and logo size are a percentage of the image width, so every image gets a watermark proportioned like the preview.

faq.q: Can I type accented characters?
faq.a: Yes. Text is drawn with the Be Vietnam Pro font, which supports accented Latin characters.

text-on-image.name: Add Text to Image
text-on-image.desc: Write text on images with your choice of font, color, outline and shadow.
howto: Choose or drag and drop an image.
Type the text, choose the font, size, color, outline and shadow; click “Add text” to add more text layers.
Drag the text into place on the image, click “Save image” and download.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Which fonts are available?
faq.a: Be Vietnam Pro, Roboto Slab, Dancing Script, Pacifico and Great Vibes, all supporting accented characters, downloaded when you pick them.

faq.q: Does the exported image match the preview?
faq.a: Yes. Text size and position scale with the image, so high-resolution originals come out exactly as you see them.

merge-images.name: Merge Images
merge-images.desc: Join multiple images horizontally, vertically or in a grid.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste 2 or more images; drag and drop to reorder.
Choose the layout (horizontal, vertical, grid), spacing, corner radius and background color.
Preview, click “Merge images” and download the merged image.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Can I merge images of different sizes?
faq.a: Yes. Turn on “Same size” to give every image the same height (horizontal) or width (vertical); in a grid, images are cropped to fill cells or kept whole.

faq.q: Can I join chat screenshots into one long image?
faq.a: Yes. Choose “Vertical” with spacing 0 to stack the screenshots seamlessly.

split-image.name: Split Image into Grid
split-image.desc: Cut one image into 2, 3, 6 or 9 tiles (for Instagram, Facebook).
howto: Choose or drag and drop an image.
Choose rows × columns (1×3, 3×3…) and see the cut lines on the image; turn on Instagram numbering if needed.
Click “Split image” and download the set as a .zip.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: In what order do I post a grid to Instagram?
faq.a: Turn on “Number in Instagram posting order”, then post images 1, 2, 3… in order; the bottom-right tile is posted first so the grid on your profile forms the original image.

faq.q: Is quality reduced?
faq.a: No downscaling: each tile keeps the original resolution of its part of the image.

favicon.name: Favicon Generator
favicon.desc: Create a .ico favicon and a full icon set for web, Apple and Android from one image.
howto: Choose a logo (ideally SVG or a square PNG of 512 px or more).
Adjust the padding, background color, corner radius and site name, and preview at 16, 32 and 180 px.
Click “Create favicon”, download the .zip and paste the HTML code into your <head> tag.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Which files are in the favicon set?
faq.a: favicon.ico (16, 32, 48 px), favicon-16x16.png, favicon-32x32.png, apple-touch-icon.png (180 px), android-chrome 192 and 512 px and site.webmanifest; plus favicon.svg if the source is an SVG.

faq.q: Why does the iPhone icon have a white background?
faq.a: iOS fills transparent areas of apple-touch-icon with black, so the tool uses your chosen background color, or white if you left it transparent.

svg-to-png.name: SVG to PNG
svg-to-png.desc: Convert SVG vector images to PNG/JPG at any resolution.
howto: Choose or drag and drop one or more SVG files.
Choose the resolution (1–8× scale, or enter a width), the PNG/JPG/WebP format and the background.
Click “Convert” and download each image or a .zip.

faq.q: Are my SVG files uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. The browser renders the SVG right on your device.

faq.q: Does enlarging an SVG make it pixelated?
faq.a: No. SVG is vector, so rendering at 4× or 8× stays sharp; the tool caps the long side at 8192 px so the browser isn't overloaded.

faq.q: Why don't images or fonts inside the SVG show?
faq.a: For security, browsers don't load images or fonts from the web when rendering an SVG to an image. Embed images and fonts (or convert text to paths) in the SVG file.

image-to-base64.name: Image to Base64
image-to-base64.desc: Convert images to Base64 strings / data URIs to embed in HTML and CSS.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste images (JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, SVG…).
Choose the output format: data URI, Base64 only, CSS, tag or Markdown.
Click “Convert to Base64”, then copy the string or download a .txt file.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: When should I embed images as Base64?
faq.a: For very small images like icons and logos under about 10 KB: it saves one file request. Keep large images as separate files, since Base64 is about 33% larger than the original.

faq.q: Does SVG need Base64?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Turn on “SVG: URL-encode” for a string about 30% shorter that still works in CSS and HTML.

color-picker.name: Image Color Picker
color-picker.desc: Tap an image to get color codes and extract its dominant palette automatically.
howto: Choose or drag and drop an image.
Hover, or tap and drag, over the image to inspect colors through the magnifier; click (or release) to pick a color; the dominant palette is extracted automatically.
Click a swatch to copy its HEX, RGB or HSL code; click “Download palette” to save an image and CSS code.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: How is the dominant palette calculated?
faq.a: The tool groups pixels with similar colors (median cut algorithm) and sorts them by area, so the color covering the most space comes first.

faq.q: Can I pick colors outside the image, on the screen?
faq.a: On desktop Chrome and Edge there's a “Pick any color on the screen” button. Other browsers don't support this yet.

gif-maker.name: GIF Maker
gif-maker.desc: Turn several images into an animated GIF, adjusting speed and size.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste 2 or more images; drag and drop to reorder the frames.
Adjust the frame duration, size, looping and back-and-forth playback, and preview the animation.
Click “Create GIF” and download the animation.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Why do the colors look a bit different?
faq.a: GIF only has up to 256 colors per frame. Photos with smooth gradients get some banding; illustrations, text and screenshots look great.

faq.q: What if the GIF is too heavy?
faq.a: Choose a smaller size (320 or 480 px) and use fewer images; the file size drops quickly.

ocr.name: Image to Text (OCR)
ocr.desc: Recognize text in photos and scans, including accented Vietnamese.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste photos, scans or scanned PDFs.
Choose the language (English or Vietnamese) and how lines are joined.
Click “Recognize text”, proofread the result, copy it or download a .txt file.

faq.q: Are images sent to a server for recognition?
faq.a: No. The Tesseract recognizer (WebAssembly) is downloaded to your browser and runs on your device.

faq.q: How accurate is it?
faq.a: Quite good with straight, sharp photos of printed text. Blurry or tilted photos and handwriting cause mistakes; proofread and fix them. You can straighten photos first with the Document Scanner.

faq.q: What about PDFs with selectable text?
faq.a: PDF to Text is faster and more accurate. OCR is for scanned PDFs (images only).

signature-extract.name: Signature & Stamp Extractor
signature-extract.desc: Extract a signature or stamp photographed on paper into a transparent PNG.
howto: Photograph the signature or stamp on white paper (straight, well lit) and choose that photo.
Choose which strokes to keep (blue for signatures, red for stamps), the output ink color and sensitivity; drag on the image to outline an area if needed.
Click “Download transparent PNG” and use it in Sign PDF, Word, Canva…

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Every step runs right in your browser; images never leave your device.

faq.q: Can a signature over a stamp be separated?
faq.a: Yes if the colors differ: choose “Blue” for just the signature, “Red” for just the stamp.

faq.q: What about shadows or yellowed paper?
faq.a: The tool estimates the paper color region by region, so it works even with uneven lighting. If smudges remain, lower the sensitivity.

faq.q: Is an extracted signature legally valid?
faq.a: A signature image is just a picture, not a digital signature. Only use your own signature and stamp, or ones you're authorized to use.

voice-recorder.name: Voice Recorder
voice-recorder.desc: Record with your microphone, pause, play back, name and download as M4A, MP3 or WAV.
voice-recorder.privacy: Audio is only recorded and kept temporarily on your device, never sent anywhere.
howto: Press the red button and allow the browser to use the microphone when asked.
Speak or play the sound to record; you can Pause and Resume.
Press the square button to stop, play it back, name it and download it as M4A, MP3 or WAV (or click Trim to cut it down).

faq.q: Are recordings sent online?
faq.a: No. Audio is recorded and kept in the browser on your device. Download it before closing or reloading the page, since recordings that aren't downloaded are lost.

faq.q: Should I turn on “Noise suppression, echo cancellation”?
faq.a: Turn it on for voice (meetings, lectures, notes) to reduce background noise. Turn it off for music and instruments to keep the natural sound.

faq.q: How long can I record?
faq.a: There's no time limit; it only depends on your device's memory. The screen stays on while recording.

screen-recorder.name: Screen Recorder
screen-recorder.desc: Record your screen, a window or a tab with system audio and microphone (on computers), download as MP4/WebM.
screen-recorder.privacy: The video is only recorded on your device and never uploaded anywhere.
howto: Choose whether to capture system/tab audio and the microphone, the quality and the format.
Click Choose a screen and start recording, then pick the entire screen, a window or a tab.
Click Stop recording (or the browser's Stop sharing), review it, then download it or send it to Trim or Compress video.

faq.q: Can I record a phone screen?
faq.a: Phone browsers don't let websites record the screen. Use the built-in feature: on iPhone, Control Center → Screen Recording; on Android, the notification shade → Screen record. Then you can use Trim video or Compress video here.

faq.q: Why does the video have no sound?
faq.a: When the browser asks to share, turn on “Share audio”. Chrome and Edge capture a tab's audio; on Windows they can capture the whole screen's audio; on macOS only tab audio. You can turn on the microphone for narration.

faq.q: Is the video sent online?
faq.a: No. Video and audio are recorded in the browser on your device; download the video before closing the page.

trim-audio.name: Trim Audio
trim-audio.desc: Cut audio clips and make ringtones (including iPhone M4R), with fade in/out effects.
howto: Choose an audio file (MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, FLAC…).
Drag the two handles on the waveform or enter the start and end times; click Play selection to listen.
Choose the format (M4R for iPhone ringtones), add fades if you like, then click Trim audio.

faq.q: Does trimming reduce quality?
faq.a: If you keep the original format and don't use fades, the data is copied as is, so quality is unchanged. When changing format or adding effects, the audio is re-encoded at the quality you choose.

faq.q: How do I make an iPhone ringtone?
faq.a: Select up to 40 seconds, choose M4R and download. Connect the iPhone to a computer, open Finder (Mac) or iTunes (Windows) and drag the .m4r file onto the iPhone; then pick it in Settings → Sounds → Ringtone.

faq.q: Is the file uploaded?
faq.a: No. The file is read and trimmed right on your device.

merge-audio.name: Merge Audio
merge-audio.desc: Join several audio files into one: back to back, with silence gaps or crossfades, with volume normalization.
howto: Choose two or more audio files (different formats are fine).
Drag and drop or use ↑↓ to order them; choose how to join and turn on Normalize volume if tracks differ in loudness.
Choose the format, click Merge audio, then listen and download.

faq.q: What is “Crossfade”?
faq.a: The end of one track fades out while the next fades in, overlapping for a few seconds, like a DJ transition. “Silence gap” inserts a few seconds of silence between tracks.

faq.q: Can I merge MP3 with M4A or WAV?
faq.a: Yes. The files are decoded and re-encoded into one file in the format you choose.

faq.q: Are files uploaded?
faq.a: No, everything happens on your device.

convert-audio.name: Audio Converter
convert-audio.desc: Convert between MP3, WAV, M4A and OGG; choose quality and mono/stereo, many files at once.
howto: Choose one or more audio files.
Choose the target format and quality (bitrate); you can switch to mono for smaller files.
Click Convert format and download each file or all of them (.zip).

faq.q: Which format should I choose?
faq.a: MP3 plays everywhere. M4A (AAC) is smaller at the same quality, good for iPhone. OGG (Opus) is the lightest. WAV is uncompressed, original quality but very large files.

faq.q: Does converting a 128 kbps MP3 to 320 kbps sound better?
faq.a: No. Quality lost in the first compression can't be restored; a higher bitrate only makes the file bigger.

faq.q: Are files uploaded?
faq.a: No. Files are converted right on your device.

video-to-mp3.name: Video to MP3
video-to-mp3.desc: Extract the audio from a video into an MP3 (or M4A, WAV), the whole video or a segment.
howto: Choose a video file (MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV).
Choose MP3 and the quality, or M4A to keep the original audio; turn on Only extract a segment if needed.
Click Extract audio, then listen and download.

faq.q: Do long, large videos work?
faq.a: Yes. The video is read piece by piece, so files of several GB work; only the audio is kept.

faq.q: How is M4A different from MP3?
faq.a: Most MP4 videos have AAC audio: with M4A the audio is copied as is, very fast with no quality loss. MP3 must be re-encoded but plays everywhere.

faq.q: Is the video uploaded?
faq.a: No. The video is processed right on your device.

video-to-gif.name: Video to GIF
video-to-gif.desc: Cut a video segment and turn it into an animated GIF, choosing size, frame rate and speed.
howto: Choose a video file.
Drag the two handles on the filmstrip to choose a segment (keep it short, a few seconds).
Choose the width, frames per second and speed, then click Create GIF.

faq.q: Why is the GIF heavier than the video?
faq.a: GIF only has 256 colors per frame and compresses much worse than video. For lighter files: a short segment, small width (320–480 px), 8–10 fps and the “Lighter” palette.

faq.q: Is the video uploaded?
faq.a: No, the animation is created right on your device.

trim-video.name: Trim Video
trim-video.desc: Cut out the part of a video you need, keeping the original quality (no re-encoding) or frame-accurate.
howto: Choose a video file (MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV).
Drag the two handles on the filmstrip or enter times; preview the selection.
Choose Fast (keeps quality) or Frame-accurate, then click Trim video.

faq.q: What's the difference between “Fast” and “Frame-accurate”?
faq.a: Fast copies video and audio as is, so it's done in seconds with no quality loss; the video starts at the chosen point in most players. Frame-accurate re-encodes the selection; it's slower, and useful when older players show a frozen frame at the start.

faq.q: Can I trim videos of several GB?
faq.a: Yes, with Fast trimming the video is read piece by piece, so it's very light.

faq.q: Is the video uploaded?
faq.a: No. The video is trimmed right on your device.

compress-video.name: Compress Video
compress-video.desc: Reduce video size for messaging and email, by quality or target size, using your device's hardware encoder.
howto: Choose a video file.
Compress by quality (High, Balanced, Smallest) or enter a target size; see the estimated size.
Click Compress video, review it, then download the MP4.

faq.q: How long does compression take?
faq.a: It depends on your device and the video length. The tool uses your device's hardware encoder through WebCodecs, so it's usually faster than the video's duration; older phones are slower. Keep the page open while compressing.

faq.q: Should I choose H.264 or H.265?
faq.a: H.264 plays everywhere. H.265 (only shown when supported) is about 30% smaller at the same quality, but older devices and apps may not play it.

faq.q: Is the video uploaded?
faq.a: No. The video is compressed right on your device.

video-frame.name: Video Frame Capture
video-frame.desc: Grab full-resolution images from any frame of a video, or capture automatically every N seconds.
howto: Choose a video file.
Seek to the spot you want, use Previous/Next frame (keys , .) to step frame by frame, click Capture this frame; or Capture the whole video every N seconds.
Choose PNG, JPG or WebP and click Download captured images.

faq.q: Are the images sharper than a screenshot?
faq.a: Yes. Images are decoded directly from the video at its original resolution (e.g. 1920×1080 or 4K), regardless of the preview size on screen.

faq.q: Is the video uploaded?
faq.a: No, images are captured right on your device.

text-to-speech.name: Text to Speech
text-to-speech.desc: Read text aloud with the voices built into your device, highlighting the current sentence, with adjustable speed.
text-to-speech.privacy: Text is read with the voices on your device; only if you choose a voice marked “online” is the text processed by that voice provider's server.
howto: Type or paste the text to read.
Choose a voice, speed and pitch.
Click Read; the current sentence is highlighted. Place the cursor mid-text to start from that sentence.

faq.q: Why is the voice wrong or missing for my language?
faq.a: Voices come from your operating system. If there's no voice for the language, the tool explains how to install one on Windows, macOS, Android or iPhone; reload the page afterwards.

faq.q: Can I download an MP3?
faq.a: No. Browsers don't let web pages record the operating system's voices, so the tool only reads aloud live.

faq.q: Is my text sent anywhere?
faq.a: Not with voices installed on your device. Voices marked “online” (like Google or Microsoft Online) send the text to the provider's server; choose another voice to keep it private.

word-counter.name: Word & Character Counter
word-counter.desc: Count words, characters, sentences, paragraphs and reading time as you type.
howto: Type or paste text into the box.
Word, character, sentence and paragraph counts and reading time update as you type.
See the most frequent words to check for repetition.

faq.q: How are words counted?
faq.a: Each group of characters separated by spaces counts as one word, the same way Word and Google Docs count.

faq.q: Is my text saved?
faq.a: It's never sent anywhere. You can turn on “Remember text” to keep it temporarily in your own browser.

case-converter.name: Case Converter
case-converter.desc: Convert to UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case or Sentence case, with full Unicode support.
howto: Type or paste text into the box.
Choose a case: UPPERCASE, lowercase, Capitalize Each Word, Sentence case or programming styles (camelCase, snake_case…).
Copy or download the result.

faq.q: Does it handle accented letters correctly?
faq.a: Yes. The tool uses Unicode case rules, so “crème brûlée” becomes “CRÈME BRÛLÉE” and back.

faq.q: Do camelCase and snake_case keep accents?
faq.a: No. Programming styles strip accents and special characters, e.g. “Phone number” becomes phoneNumber or phone_number.

slugify.name: Slug Generator
slugify.desc: Create URL-friendly slugs from titles, removing accents.
howto: Type article titles, one per line.
Choose the separator and maximum length.
Copy the slugs to use in your URLs.

faq.q: What is a slug?
faq.a: The readable part of a page's URL, e.g. “how-to-install” in example.com/how-to-install. Slugs without accents, in lowercase, joined by hyphens are easier to share and better for SEO.

faq.q: Does the length limit cut words in half?
faq.a: No, the tool backs up to the nearest separator so no word is cut in two.

text-diff.name: Text Compare (Diff)
text-diff.desc: Find the differences between two texts, highlighting additions and deletions.
howto: Paste the original into the left box and the new version into the right box.
Compare by lines, words or characters; view side by side or unified.
Additions are green, deletions red; long identical sections are collapsed.

faq.q: Is my text sent to a server to compare?
faq.a: No. The diff algorithm (Myers) runs right in your browser.

faq.q: Should I compare by lines or by words?
faq.a: Contracts and source code are best compared by lines (changed words within a line are still highlighted). Flowing prose is best compared by words.

dedupe-lines.name: Remove Duplicate Lines & Sort
dedupe-lines.desc: Remove duplicate and empty lines, sort A→Z, reverse or shuffle lines.
howto: Paste a list, one item per line.
Choose the sort order and turn removal of duplicates and empty lines on or off.
See how many lines were removed, then copy the result.

faq.q: Is the A→Z sort correct for accented letters?
faq.a: Yes: accented letters sort next to their base letters, and numbers are compared by value (file2 comes before file10).

faq.q: Are “An” and “an” treated as duplicates?
faq.a: Yes when “Case-insensitive” is on; the first occurrence is kept.

find-replace.name: Find and Replace
find-replace.desc: Find and replace in bulk, with regular expression (regex) support.
howto: Paste the text into the box.
Enter the text to find and its replacement; choose match case, whole words or regex.
Replaced spots are highlighted; copy or download the result.

faq.q: How do I use regular expressions?
faq.a: Turn on “Regular expression”, use $1, $2 or $<name> to insert captured groups and \n for a line break. Click “Sample” for an example that turns 10/21/2026 into 2026-10-21.

faq.q: Can a bad expression freeze the page?
faq.a: No, the expression runs in a separate thread and stops automatically after a few seconds if it loops too long.

fancy-text.name: Fancy Text Generator
fancy-text.desc: Create fancy text (𝓫𝓮𝓪𝓾𝓽𝓲𝓯𝓾𝓵) for Facebook, TikTok and Instagram bios.
howto: Type a name or a short phrase.
More than 20 styles appear right below.
Click the style you like to copy it, then paste it into Facebook, TikTok or Instagram.

faq.q: Is this a font?
faq.a: No, these are special Unicode characters (mathematical letters, circled letters…), so they keep their style wherever you paste them, no font installation needed.

faq.q: Do accented letters look good?
faq.a: Accents are kept, but some devices place them off-center on styled letters. Preview before posting; Strikethrough, Spaced and Fullwidth keep accents best.

faq.q: Should I use it as a display name?
faq.a: Screen readers for blind users read these characters very poorly, and some platforms block unusual characters in account names.

markdown-to-html.name: Markdown to HTML
markdown-to-html.desc: Convert Markdown to HTML with a live preview.
howto: Type or paste Markdown into the left box.
See the preview on the right, or switch to “HTML code”.
Copy the HTML or download it as a complete .html file.

faq.q: What syntax is supported?
faq.a: Standard Markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown: tables, strikethrough, task lists, code blocks.

faq.q: Is the preview safe from malicious code?
faq.a: Yes, the preview is sanitized with DOMPurify (removing scripts and event attributes). The exported HTML keeps exactly what the Markdown produced.

percentage.name: Percentage Calculator
percentage.desc: X% of Y, X is what percent of Y, percentage increase/decrease.
howto: Choose a calculation: X% of Y, X is what % of Y, percent change, add/subtract a percentage, or find the original number.
Enter two numbers.
The result and how it's calculated appear right away; copy the link to share it.

faq.q: How do I calculate a percentage change?
faq.a: (new value − old value) ÷ old value × 100. For example, from 80 to 100 is a 25% increase.

faq.q: A price includes 10%; what was the original price?
faq.a: Choose “X is Y% of what number”, enter the increased price as X and Y = 110; don't just subtract 10%.

discount.name: Discount Calculator
discount.desc: Price after discount, stacked discounts and how much you save.
howto: Enter the original price.
Enter the discount as a percentage (for stacked discounts write 20+10) or an amount off.
See the price to pay, how much you save and the real total discount.

faq.q: Is 20% off then another 10% off the same as 30% off?
faq.a: No. The second discount applies to the reduced price, so the total is only 28%: 100 → 80 → 72.

compound-interest.name: Compound Interest Calculator
compound-interest.desc: Calculate compound interest with regular contributions, with a growth chart.
howto: Enter the initial deposit, the monthly contribution, the annual rate and the number of years.
Choose the compounding frequency (yearly, quarterly, monthly, daily).
See the final value, the interest earned and the yearly growth chart; download the table as CSV.

faq.q: What is compound interest?
faq.a: Interest that is added to the principal so it earns interest itself in the next period. The longer the time, the bigger the interest compared to what you put in.

faq.q: What is the rule of 72?
faq.a: Divide 72 by the annual rate (%) to get roughly how many years it takes for money to double. At 8% a year, about 9 years.

split-bill.name: Split the Bill
split-bill.desc: Who paid what and who owes whom — with the fewest possible transfers.
howto: Add the names of the group members.
Add each expense: who paid, how much, and who it's split between (uncheck people who didn't take part).
See who needs to pay whom with the fewest transfers; click “Copy link” to send it to the group.

faq.q: Do I need an account?
faq.a: No. The whole split lives in the link itself; send the link to the group and anyone can open it.

faq.q: How is the minimum number of transfers calculated?
faq.a: The tool works out how much each person overpaid or underpaid, then matches the person who owes the most with the one owed the most until everything is settled. A group of n people needs at most n − 1 transfers.

unit-converter.name: Unit Converter
unit-converter.desc: Length, mass, temperature, area, volume, speed, data and more.
howto: Choose a quantity: length, mass, temperature, area, volume, speed, time, data, pressure, energy.
Enter a value and choose the source and target units (click ⇄ to swap).
The table below converts to every unit of that kind.

faq.q: How many cm is 1 inch?
faq.a: 1 inch = 2.54 cm; 1 foot = 30.48 cm; 1 mile = 1.609 km.

faq.q: How do I convert °F to °C?
Is 1 GB 1000 or 1024 MB?
faq.a: In SI units, 1 GB = 1000 MB, while 1 GiB = 1024 MiB. Windows shows sizes in GiB but labels them GB, so a 1 TB drive shows about 931 GB.

age-calculator.name: Age Calculator
age-calculator.desc: Your exact age in years, months and days, and the countdown to your next birthday.
howto: Choose your date of birth.
Change “Age at date” to find your age on a date other than today.
See your exact age in years, months and days, total days and weeks, and the days until your next birthday.

faq.q: If I was born on February 29, when is my birthday in non-leap years?
faq.a: The tool uses February 28 in non-leap years.

faq.q: What is the “East Asian age” shown?
faq.a: Your age as counted traditionally in Vietnam and East Asia: by lunar years, starting at 1 at birth. The main result is your actual age.

date-calculator.name: Date Calculator & Business Days
date-calculator.desc: Days between two dates, add or subtract days, and count business days.
howto: Choose “Days between two dates” to count the days, weeks, months and working days between two dates.
Or choose “Add / subtract days” to find the date N days, working days, weeks, months or years before or after.
Optionally treat Saturday as a working day and exclude Vietnam's public holidays and days off in lieu.

faq.q: Which holidays can be excluded?
faq.a: Vietnam's public holidays: New Year's Day, 5 days of Lunar New Year, Hung Kings' Day (10th day of the 3rd lunar month), April 30, May 1, National Day (September 1–2), and Vietnam Culture Day on November 24 from 2026.

faq.q: Are swapped working days taken into account?
faq.a: Not yet. Swapped working days are announced each year and can differ between public agencies and businesses.

bmi.name: BMI Calculator
bmi.desc: Body Mass Index with Asian and WHO international classifications.
howto: Enter your height (cm) and weight (kg).
Choose the Asian classification (default) or the international WHO standard.
See your BMI, its category and the healthy weight range for your height.

faq.q: What is a normal BMI?
faq.a: WHO: 18.5 to under 25 is normal, 25–30 overweight, 30+ obese. For Asians: 18.5 to under 23 is normal, 23 to under 25 overweight, 25+ obese.

faq.q: Why do Asians use different thresholds?
faq.a: At the same BMI, Asians usually have more body fat and a higher, earlier risk of heart disease and diabetes, so the WHO recommends lower thresholds for the Asia-Pacific region.

tdee.name: TDEE Calorie Calculator
tdee.desc: Calculate BMR, TDEE and the calories to maintain, lose or gain weight.
howto: Choose your sex and enter your age, height and weight.
Choose the activity level closest to yours.
See your BMR, TDEE and the daily calories to maintain, lose or gain weight.

faq.q: What's the difference between BMR and TDEE?
faq.a: BMR is the energy your body needs at complete rest; TDEE is your total daily energy expenditure, including activity. Eating at your TDEE maintains your weight.

faq.q: How much should I eat to lose 0.5 kg a week?
faq.a: About 550 kcal a day below your TDEE (1 kg of fat ≈ 7,700 kcal). Don't lose more than 1 kg a week or eat below 1,200 kcal (women) or 1,500 kcal (men) without medical supervision.

due-date.name: Due Date Calculator
due-date.desc: Your due date and weeks of pregnancy from the first day of your last period.
howto: Enter the first day of your last period and your cycle length (or calculate from an ultrasound).
See your due date, today's gestational age and trimester.
The checkup table shows the date ranges for common prenatal visits and scans.

faq.q: How is the due date calculated?
faq.a: With Naegele's rule: the first day of the last period + 280 days (40 weeks), adjusted if your cycle is longer or shorter than 28 days.

faq.q: Should I trust my last period or the ultrasound?
faq.a: A first-trimester ultrasound (crown-rump length) is usually more accurate when you don't remember the date or your cycles are irregular; your doctor decides the final due date.

scientific-calculator.name: Scientific Calculator
scientific-calculator.desc: Calculator with sin, cos, log, powers and history, usable from the keyboard.
howto: Click the buttons or type the calculation on the keyboard (Enter to calculate, Esc to clear).
Choose degrees (DEG) or radians (RAD) for sin, cos, tan.
Click a line in the history to reuse it; the Ans button inserts the previous result.

faq.q: What does 200 + 10% give?
faq.a: 220, like a pocket calculator: the percentage is taken of the number before it. And 50% × 200 = 100.

faq.q: Can I write 2π or 2sin30?
faq.a: Yes. Implicit multiplication works: 2π, 3(4+5), 2sin30.

faq.q: Is the history sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. Calculation history is only stored in the browser on your device.

roman-numerals.name: Roman Numeral Converter
roman-numerals.desc: Convert numbers to Roman numerals and back.
howto: Type numbers (1–3,999,999) or Roman numerals, one per line.
The tool detects the direction and shows the results right away.
Copy or download them.

faq.q: What's the largest Roman numeral?
faq.a: In standard notation, 3,999 (MMMCMXCIX). Larger numbers use an overline to multiply by 1,000, e.g. V̅ = 5,000.

faq.q: Why is IIII marked as wrong?
faq.a: Standard notation uses subtraction: 4 is IV, 9 is IX, 40 is XL, 90 is XC… IIII only appears on clock faces.

qr-generator.name: QR Code Generator
qr-generator.desc: Create QR codes for links, text, WiFi, contact cards (vCard), SMS and email; change colors, add a logo, download PNG/SVG.
howto: Choose the content type: link, text, WiFi, contact card, SMS, email or phone.
Enter the details; the QR code updates instantly.
Change colors, add a logo if you like, then download PNG/SVG or copy the image.

faq.q: Do the QR codes expire?
faq.a: No. The QR code contains your content directly, without any redirect link, so it works forever.

faq.q: Does a logo make it harder to scan?
faq.a: With a logo, the tool automatically uses the highest error correction (H) so it still scans. Keep the logo under about 20% of the code's width.

faq.q: Is the WiFi password saved in the share link?
faq.a: No. The password is only in the QR code on your device, never in the share link.

qr-scanner.name: QR Code Scanner
qr-scanner.desc: Scan QR codes and barcodes with your camera, from screenshots or PDF files.
howto: Click “Turn camera on” and point it at a QR code, or choose/paste an image or PDF containing one.
The result appears instantly; links, WiFi, contact cards and payment codes are broken down for you.
Copy the content or open the link (always check the address carefully before opening).

faq.q: Is the camera image sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. Each frame is decoded on your device with WebAssembly or the browser's built-in feature.

faq.q: Which codes can it read?
faq.a: QR, Micro QR, Data Matrix, Aztec, PDF417 and common barcodes such as EAN-13, Code 128, Code 39 and UPC.

barcode-generator.name: Barcode Generator
barcode-generator.desc: Create EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, ITF-14, Code 128 and Code 39 barcodes; auto check digits, batch creation and printable label PDFs.
howto: Choose the type: EAN-13 for retail products, Code 128 for internal codes and shipping labels, ITF-14 for cartons…
Enter the content (for EAN/UPC just the digits, the check digit is added automatically) or paste a whole list to create many codes.
Download PNG/SVG, copy the image, or click “Print labels” for an A4 PDF with the codes laid out.

faq.q: Can I sell products in stores with an EAN-13 I make myself?
faq.a: To sell in retail stores, a business must register a GS1 company prefix with its national GS1 organization before numbering products. The tool only draws a standards-compliant barcode from the digits you enter.

faq.q: Will the codes scan?
faq.a: Codes are drawn to each type's standard and verified with the ZXing decoder. When printing, keep a white background and black bars, leave quiet zones on both sides and don't shrink too much (3 px per bar or more).

faq.q: Does Code 128 accept accented letters?
faq.a: No. Code 128 and Code 39 only encode ASCII characters; remove accents or use a QR code if you need them.

excel-viewer.name: Excel & CSV Viewer
excel-viewer.desc: Open .xlsx, .xls, .ods and .csv files without Excel; switch sheets, search, filter and sort.
howto: Choose, drag and drop or paste an Excel/CSV file.
Click a sheet name to switch sheets; type in the search box (accents optional) to filter rows, or choose a column to search only in it.
Click a column header to sort, click a cell to see its full content and formula; download the filtered view as Excel or CSV.

faq.q: Is my Excel file uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. The file is read right in your browser with the SheetJS library; no server receives your file.

faq.q: CSV accented characters look garbled?
faq.a: The tool auto-detects UTF-8 or Windows code pages and comma, semicolon or tab delimiters, so text displays correctly.

faq.q: What about formulas and formatting?
faq.a: Formula cells show the value already calculated in the file; click a cell to see the formula. Colors, borders, images and charts aren't shown since the tool only reads data.

excel-csv.name: Excel ↔ CSV Converter
excel-csv.desc: Convert Excel to UTF-8 CSV without garbled characters (one file per sheet) and CSV to Excel, keeping leading zeros.
howto: Choose one or more Excel (.xlsx, .xls, .ods) or CSV files.
Excel → CSV: choose the sheets and delimiter; CSV → Excel: turn on number detection and optionally combine several CSVs into one file.
Click “Convert” and download each file or all of them as a .zip.

faq.q: Why does a CSV look garbled in Excel?
faq.a: Excel only reads UTF-8 correctly when the file starts with a BOM. The tool adds one (you can turn it off), so Excel opens it without garbled characters.

faq.q: Do phone numbers starting with 0 lose the zero?
faq.a: No. When converting CSV to Excel, numbers with leading zeros and numbers longer than 15 digits (IDs, account numbers) are kept as text.

faq.q: Comma or semicolon?
faq.a: If your computer uses a comma as the decimal separator (many European locales), Excel needs semicolons. Other software, Google Sheets and programming usually use commas.

merge-excel.name: Merge Excel Files
merge-excel.desc: Combine multiple Excel/CSV files or sheets into one table, lining up same-named columns and adding a source column.
howto: Choose the Excel/CSV files to merge (drag and drop to reorder).
Choose “Stack into one table” (same-named columns lined up, with a Source column) or “Keep each sheet separate”.
Click “Merge files”, preview, then download the Excel or CSV file.

faq.q: What if the files have columns in different orders?
faq.a: With “First row is the header” on, columns are matched by name (case- and accent-insensitive), so the order doesn't matter; columns only in one file are added at the end.

faq.q: Are formulas kept?
faq.a: Formula cells are copied as their calculated values, since cell positions change after merging and the formulas would break.

split-excel.name: Split Excel by Column
split-excel.desc: Split one table into several sheets or Excel/CSV files by the values of a column (branch, department…).
howto: Choose an Excel or CSV file.
Choose the sheet and the column to split by (the tool suggests suitable columns); the list of parts and row counts appears right away.
Choose the output: one file with many sheets, many Excel files or many CSV files, then click “Split file”.

faq.q: Are values with different letter case split separately?
faq.a: No. “New York” and “new york ” are grouped together (extra spaces trimmed, case-insensitive); empty cells go into the “Empty” part.

faq.q: Does each part keep the header row?
faq.a: Yes, with “First row is the header” on, every file/sheet gets the header row and a filter.

json-excel.name: JSON ↔ Excel Converter
json-excel.desc: Convert JSON arrays into Excel tables (flattening nested objects) and Excel/CSV into JSON.
howto: Choose a .json file (to get Excel) or an Excel/CSV file (to get JSON).
Options: flatten nested objects into “a.b” columns, or the reverse, build nested objects from dotted column names.
Click “Convert”, preview, then download the file or copy the JSON.

faq.q: What if the JSON has several lists?
faq.a: If the JSON is an object containing several arrays (e.g. “employees” and “departments”), each array becomes its own sheet.

faq.q: How do Excel dates come out in JSON?
faq.a: Date cells are written in standard ISO “yyyy-mm-dd” form (with the time if the cell has one); numbers stay numbers.

mail-merge.name: Mail Merge
mail-merge.desc: Create letters and invitations in bulk from an Excel/CSV list and a Word (.docx) or text template: one DOCX per person, a combined DOCX for printing, or PDF.
howto: Choose an Excel/CSV list (first row = column names) and a Word template with fields like {{Full name}} together; or choose “Type a text template”.
Check which fields match columns, choose the column for file names and preview each person.
Click “Mail merge” to download one file per person (.zip), one combined Word file for printing, or PDF.

faq.q: How do I write fields in the Word file?
faq.a: Type the column name in double curly braces like {{Full name}} or «Full name», matching the column name in the Excel file (case- and accent-insensitive). Mail Merge fields (MERGEFIELD) created in Word also work. Text formatting (bold, color) applied to a field is kept.

faq.q: Can it export PDF directly from a Word template?
faq.a: Browsers can't accurately rebuild Word layouts as PDF, so for Word templates the tool exports .docx (including a combined version to print in one go; open it in Word or Google Docs and save as PDF). For typed templates, it exports PDF directly.

faq.q: Is my list sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. Both the Excel and Word files are processed right on your device.

email-signature.name: Email Signature Generator
email-signature.desc: Create a professional HTML email signature for Gmail and Outlook with photo, logo and social links, ready to paste.
howto: Enter your name, job title, company, phone, email and website; add photo, logo and social links if you like.
Choose the layout, accent color and font; preview it as in a real email.
Click “Copy signature” and paste it into the signature settings of Gmail or Outlook (step-by-step instructions included).

faq.q: Why must images be links?
faq.a: Gmail and Outlook don't keep images embedded in a pasted signature; images must live at a public address (https://…), such as your company website.

faq.q: Is my information saved?
faq.a: Only remembered in this device's browser so it's there next time; never sent anywhere. Click “Reset” to clear it.

json-formatter.name: JSON Formatter & Validator
json-formatter.desc: Beautify, minify, sort keys and validate JSON, pointing to the exact line/column of errors.
howto: Paste JSON into the left box.
The formatted result appears instantly; syntax errors show the line, column and offending part.
Choose the indentation, minify or sort keys, then copy or download a .json file.

faq.q: Is my JSON sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Everything uses JSON.parse right in your browser.

faq.q: Can it fix “almost valid” JSON?
faq.a: There's a light repair option: remove // comments and trailing commas, and turn single quotes into double quotes.

json-convert.name: JSON ↔ CSV/YAML Converter
json-convert.desc: Convert back and forth between JSON, CSV and YAML.
howto: Paste JSON, CSV or YAML into the left box.
Choose the target format (and the CSV delimiter if needed).
Copy or download the result.

faq.q: How is nested JSON converted to CSV?
faq.a: Child objects are flattened into columns like “contact.email”; converting the CSV back to JSON rebuilds the nested structure.

faq.q: The CSV opens in a single column in Excel?
faq.a: Excel on computers using a comma as the decimal separator expects semicolons. Choose “Semicolon (;)” before downloading.

faq.q: Do phone numbers lose their leading zero?
faq.a: No, values with a leading zero are kept as strings when converting CSV to JSON.

base64.name: Base64 Encode/Decode
base64.desc: Encode and decode Base64 for UTF-8 text and files.
howto: Choose the direction: encode or decode.
Type or paste text, or click “File” to encode a file.
If the Base64 string is an image, PDF…, click “Save as file” to download it.

faq.q: Is Base64 secure encryption?
faq.a: No. Base64 only turns data into safe characters for transport; anyone can decode it. Use real encryption to keep things secret.

faq.q: Does accented text decode correctly?
faq.a: Yes, the tool uses UTF-8, so accented letters and emoji are kept. It also accepts URL-safe Base64 (- _) and strings missing the = padding.

url-encode.name: URL Encode/Decode
url-encode.desc: Encode/decode URLs (percent-encoding) and break down query parameters.
howto: Choose encode or decode.
Paste a URL or text; for URLs, see the table of parts and decoded parameters.
Copy the result or individual parameters.

faq.q: What's the difference between “One parameter” and “Whole URL”?
faq.a: “One parameter” also encodes / ? & = (for a value placed after =). “Whole URL” keeps the structural characters so the link still works.

faq.q: Why does + become a space?
faq.a: In form data, spaces are encoded as +. Turn off “Turn + into spaces” if the + is real.

html-entity.name: HTML Entity Encoder
html-entity.desc: Convert special characters to HTML entities and back.
howto: Choose encode or decode.
Paste HTML or text; choose what to encode and the entity format.
Copy the result.

faq.q: When do I need HTML entities?
faq.a: When you want to show HTML code literally on a page (e.g. in a tutorial) or insert user data into HTML without it being parsed as tags.

faq.q: Do accented letters need encoding?
faq.a: Not on UTF-8 pages. Only encode non-ASCII characters for old systems without UTF-8 support.

jwt-decoder.name: JWT Decoder
jwt-decoder.desc: View a JWT's header, payload and expiry; verify HMAC and public-key signatures.
howto: Paste a JWT (with or without “Bearer”).
See the header, payload and expiry times.
Enter the secret (HS256…) or public key (RS256, ES256…) to verify the signature.

faq.q: Is it safe to paste a real token here?
faq.a: The token is only decoded and verified in your browser, never sent anywhere. Still, be careful with valid tokens from real systems.

faq.q: What's the sample token's key?
faq.a: The sample token is signed with HS256 using the key “bbetools-bi-mat”. Change one character of the key to see the signature fail.

faq.q: Which algorithms can be verified?
faq.a: HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, PS256/384/512, ES256/384/512 and EdDSA (in browsers supporting Ed25519). Public keys are accepted as PEM or JWK.

uuid.name: UUID Generator
uuid.desc: Generate UUID v4 and v7 in bulk.
howto: Choose version v4 or v7 and how many.
Choose uppercase, hyphens or braces if needed.
Copy or download the list; paste a UUID into the inspect box to see its version and creation time.

faq.q: Should I use UUID v4 or v7?
faq.a: v4 is fully random. v7 starts with the creation time, so it's increasing, which makes database indexes faster when used as a primary key.

faq.q: Can UUIDs collide?
faq.a: Practically never: UUID v4 has 122 random bits, generated with the browser's crypto.getRandomValues.

hash.name: Hash Generator (MD5/SHA)
hash.desc: Calculate MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 hashes of text.
howto: Type or paste text.
MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 appear instantly; enter a key to calculate an HMAC.
Paste an existing hash into “Compare with” to check for a match.

faq.q: Why is my hash different from another tool?
faq.a: Hashes are very sensitive: a single space or trailing newline changes the result completely. The tool hashes the UTF-8 text exactly as it is in the box.

faq.q: Can a hash be reversed into text?
faq.a: No. Hashes are one-way; they can only be guessed, which is why weak passwords are still easy to crack.

regex-tester.name: Regex Tester
regex-tester.desc: Test regular expressions with highlighted matches and capture groups.
howto: Enter the expression (abc or /abc/gi) and choose flags.
Paste test text: matches are highlighted and a table lists each capture group.
Enter a replacement string to preview the replace result.

faq.q: Which regex flavor is used?
faq.a: JavaScript (ECMAScript) syntax, similar to Python, PHP and Java for the basics. Turn on the u flag to use \p{L} (any letter, including accented ones).

faq.q: What if an expression runs forever?
faq.a: The expression runs in a separate thread and is stopped after 2.5 seconds, so the page never freezes.

timestamp.name: Unix Timestamp Converter
timestamp.desc: Convert Unix timestamps ↔ dates in your local time zone and UTC.
howto: Paste a Unix timestamp (seconds, milliseconds…) or a date/time.
See the date in your local time, UTC, ISO 8601 and how long ago (or from now) it is.
Click the copy icon next to the format you need.

faq.q: What is a Unix timestamp?
faq.a: The number of seconds since 00:00:00 UTC on January 1, 1970. For example, 1767225600 is 00:00 UTC on January 1, 2026.

faq.q: How do I know if it's seconds or milliseconds?
faq.a: The tool detects it from the length: 10 digits is seconds, 13 milliseconds, 16 microseconds, 19 nanoseconds.

cron.name: Cron Expression Explainer
cron.desc: Explain cron expressions in plain English and list the next run times.
howto: Paste a cron expression (or a whole crontab line with the command).
Read the plain-English explanation and the meaning of each field.
See the next 10 runs in your local time, UTC or Vietnam time.

faq.q: What are cron's five fields?
faq.a: In order: minute (0–59), hour (0–23), day of month (1–31), month (1–12), day of week (0–6, 0 is Sunday). 6-field expressions add seconds at the start.

faq.q: The server runs at the wrong time?
faq.a: Servers are usually set to UTC, which may differ from your local time. Choose “UTC” to see exactly when the server will run it.
