color-converter.name: Color Converter
color-converter.desc: Convert HEX, RGB, HSL and OKLCH; check text/background contrast.
howto: Type a color code in any format or use the color picker.
Copy the HEX, RGB, HSL, OKLCH… format you need.
Choose a background color to check text contrast against WCAG.

faq.q: What contrast ratio passes?
faq.a: Per WCAG, normal text needs at least 4.5:1 (AA) and large text 3:1; AAA is 7:1 and 4.5:1.

faq.q: What is OKLCH?
faq.a: A newer CSS color space with more perceptually even lightness than HSL; all modern browsers support oklch().

faq.q: Can I use the CMYK values for printing?
faq.a: They're only an approximation. Real print colors depend on the printer's color profile; ask your printer when accuracy matters.

css-generator.name: CSS Gradient & Box-Shadow Generator
css-generator.desc: Visually adjust gradients, box-shadows and border-radius, then copy the CSS.
howto: Choose an effect: gradient, box-shadow or border radius.
Drag the sliders, pick colors and see the preview instantly.
Click “Copy CSS” and paste it into your CSS file.

faq.q: Does the CSS work in every browser?
faq.a: Yes, gradients, box-shadow and border-radius are supported by all modern browsers without -webkit- prefixes.

faq.q: Why use two shadow layers?
faq.a: A wide, faint layer plus a close, sharper one feels more natural than a single shadow.

sql-formatter.name: SQL Formatter
sql-formatter.desc: Beautify SQL statements (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server…).
howto: Paste an SQL statement.
Choose the database, keyword case and indentation.
Copy or download a .sql file.

faq.q: Is my query sent to a server?
faq.a: No, formatting runs with the sql-formatter library right in your browser.

faq.q: Can formatting change the meaning of the query?
faq.a: No, the tool only changes whitespace, line breaks and keyword case; quoted strings stay the same.

minifier.name: JS/CSS/HTML Minifier
minifier.desc: Minify JavaScript, CSS and HTML code to reduce size.
howto: Paste JavaScript, CSS, HTML or JSON code.
Let it auto-detect the language or choose it.
See how many percent smaller it got, then copy or download.

faq.q: What does it use to minify?
faq.a: JavaScript uses Terser, CSS uses CSSO, and HTML collapses whitespace, removes comments and minifies inline scripts/styles. Everything runs in the browser.

faq.q: Does minified code behave like the original?
faq.a: Yes, it only removes whitespace and comments and shortens local variable names. Keep the original for future edits.

base-converter.name: Number Base Converter
base-converter.desc: Convert numbers between binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal and any base.
howto: Type a number and choose its base (decimal, hex, binary…).
Results in other bases appear instantly, with digits grouped for readability.
Negative numbers also get two's complement forms from 8 to 64 bits.

faq.q: How large can numbers be?
faq.a: Unlimited: the tool uses BigInt, so numbers with hundreds of digits stay exact.

faq.q: Can it convert fractional numbers?
faq.a: Currently only integers are supported.

chmod.name: Chmod Calculator
chmod.desc: Convert Linux file permissions between numeric (755) and rwx forms.
howto: Type permissions as a number (755) or symbols (rwxr-xr-x), or tick the permission table.
See the numeric and symbolic forms and an explanation for each user group.
Enter a file name to get a ready-made chmod command to copy.

faq.q: What's the difference between 755 and 644?
faq.a: 755: the owner can read/write/execute, others can read and execute (folders, scripts). 644: the owner can read/write, others can only read (regular files).

faq.q: Should I use 777?
faq.a: No. 777 lets every user on the machine write to the file, which is easy to abuse.

user-agent.name: User-Agent Parser
user-agent.desc: See the browser, operating system and device from a User-Agent string.
howto: The box is prefilled with your browser's User-Agent; paste another string if needed.
See the browser, operating system and device type.
For this device, also see the screen, language and time zone.

faq.q: Why does Windows 11 show as Windows 10?
faq.a: Windows 11's User-Agent still says “Windows NT 10.0”. On Chrome and Edge, the tool also reads Client Hints to detect Windows 11 correctly.

faq.q: Does it detect in-app browsers?
faq.a: Yes, the tool says when the page is opened inside apps like Facebook, Instagram, TikTok or Zalo.

http-status.name: HTTP Status Codes
http-status.desc: What 1xx–5xx codes (404, 500, 301…) mean, explained in plain English.
howto: Type a code (404, 5xx) or a keyword like “not found” or “timeout”.
Filter by class 1xx–5xx.
Read the explanation and how to fix common errors.

faq.q: What's the difference between 4xx and 5xx errors?
faq.a: 4xx are errors on the request side (wrong address, missing permission, bad data). 5xx are server-side errors; users can usually only wait and retry.

faq.q: 301 or 302 for a redirect?
faq.a: Use 301 (or 308) for permanent moves so Google transfers ranking to the new page; 302 (or 307) for temporary ones.

password-generator.name: Strong Password Generator
password-generator.desc: Generate secure random passwords, memorable passphrases or PINs with the browser's secure random generator.
password-generator.privacy: Passwords are generated right in your browser with a secure random generator; they're never saved or sent anywhere.
howto: Choose a type: random, memorable passphrase or PIN.
Drag the length slider and choose character types; new passwords appear instantly.
Click Copy and paste it into the sign-up page or your password manager.

faq.q: Are passwords saved or sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. Passwords are generated with crypto.getRandomValues (a cryptographic random generator) on your device; BbeTools never stores or sends them.

faq.q: How long should a password be?
faq.a: At least 12 random characters, preferably 16 or more; passphrases should have 5–6 words. Use a different password for each account.

faq.q: What is a memorable passphrase?
faq.a: A few common English words picked at random and joined together (e.g. River-Cloud-Tiger-…), easy to remember and type on a phone but still hard to guess because there are trillions of combinations.

password-strength.name: Password Strength Checker
password-strength.desc: Estimate how long a password takes to crack, find predictable patterns (common passwords, names, dates, keyboard walks) and get tips to improve.
password-strength.privacy: The password is only checked in this browser; it's never saved or sent anywhere.
howto: Type or paste a password into the box.
See its strength, the time to crack it and any predictable patterns found.
Follow the tips, or use the Strong Password Generator.

faq.q: Is it safe to type my real password here?
faq.a: The check runs entirely in the browser: the password is never saved or sent. Still, it's a good habit to test a similar password instead.

faq.q: How is the crack time calculated?
faq.a: With the zxcvbn library: it estimates the number of guesses from leaked password lists, names, common words (plus a Vietnamese dictionary), keyboard patterns, dates… then divides by the guessing speed of each attack type.

faq.q: Does it check breached passwords (Have I Been Pwned)?
faq.a: No. That would require sending part of the password's hash to another server, against BbeTools' rule of never sending data.

file-encrypt.name: Encrypt / Decrypt Files
file-encrypt.desc: Lock any file with a password (AES-GCM 256, WebCrypto) and unlock it when needed.
howto: Choose one or more files (regular files are encrypted, .bbe files are decrypted).
Enter a password (re-enter it to confirm when encrypting).
Click Encrypt / Decrypt and download the result.

faq.q: Which algorithm is used?
faq.a: 256-bit AES-GCM through the browser's Web Crypto; the key is derived from the password with PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations and a random salt. The file is split into 1 MB blocks, each with an authentication tag, so modifying or truncating even one byte is detected.

faq.q: Can I recover the file if I forget the password?
faq.a: No. There's no back door; not even BbeTools can open it.

faq.q: How does the recipient open a .bbe file?
faq.a: Open BbeTools' Encrypt/Decrypt Files page in any browser, choose the .bbe file and enter the right password. The original file name is stored (encrypted) inside.

faq.q: Do large files work?
faq.a: Yes, files are processed in 1 MB blocks. The practical limit depends on your device's memory (usually several GB on a computer).

text-encrypt.name: Encrypt Text
text-encrypt.desc: Encrypt messages with a password (AES-GCM) to send over insecure channels.
text-encrypt.privacy: Text and password are only processed in your browser and never sent anywhere.
howto: Type a message and set a password: the Base64 ciphertext appears instantly.
Send the ciphertext (or the decryption link) by message or email; share the password through another channel.
The recipient chooses Decrypt, pastes the ciphertext and enters the password to read it.

faq.q: Who can read the encrypted message?
faq.a: Only someone with the right password. The ciphertext uses 256-bit AES-GCM with a key derived by PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations; changing a single character of the ciphertext is detected.

faq.q: Does the decryption link contain the password?
faq.a: No. The link only contains the ciphertext, after the # so browsers don't send it to the server. Whoever opens the link still has to enter the password.

faq.q: Why is the output different every time?
faq.a: Each encryption uses a new random nonce, so the same message gives a different ciphertext. That's normal and more secure.

checksum.name: File Checksum Calculator
checksum.desc: Calculate SHA-256, SHA-1, MD5, SHA-512 and CRC32 of files (even several GB) and compare with the hash on the download page.
howto: Choose the file to check (files of several GB work).
Choose the algorithms; paste the hash from the download page into the compare box, or drop a .sha256 / .md5 file alongside.
Click Calculate checksum: the result says Matches or Doesn't match.

faq.q: What is a checksum for?
faq.a: To make sure a downloaded file is intact and hasn't been corrupted or replaced: calculate its hash and compare it with the one published by the vendor. A single wrong byte gives a completely different hash.

faq.q: Should I use MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256?
faq.a: Use the algorithm the download page provides. If you can choose, prefer SHA-256: MD5 and SHA-1 are only good for detecting download errors, not deliberate tampering.

faq.q: Is the file uploaded?
faq.a: No. The file is read piece by piece on your device, even very large ones.

totp.name: 2FA Code Generator (TOTP)
totp.desc: Generate 6-digit authentication codes from a 2FA secret key, like Google Authenticator.
totp.privacy: The secret key stays only in the browser: not saved, not put in the link, never sent anywhere.
howto: Paste the secret key (Base32) or an otpauth:// link, or click Read from QR image.
The 6-digit code appears instantly and changes every 30 seconds.
Click Copy and paste it into the 2-step verification box.

faq.q: Can it replace Google Authenticator?
faq.a: It shouldn't. The tool doesn't save keys, so closing the page loses them; use it for testing, checking or temporarily recovering from a backed-up key. For daily use, install an authenticator app on your phone.

faq.q: The code doesn't match the website?
faq.a: Check that your device's clock is correct (TOTP is time-based), and that the digits / period / algorithm match the service's settings (usually 6 digits, 30 seconds, SHA-1).

faq.q: What is the Generate a new key button for?
faq.a: For developers testing 2-step login: it creates a random 160-bit key with a QR code to scan in an authenticator app.

pomodoro.name: Pomodoro Timer
pomodoro.desc: A 25-minute focus, 5-minute break timer using the Pomodoro technique, with sounds, notifications and daily stats.
howto: Write what you're working on (optional) and click Start or press Space.
Work until the bell rings, then take a 5-minute short break; after 4 sessions take a long break.
Adjust durations, sounds and auto-start in Settings.

faq.q: Does the timer keep running if I close the tab?
faq.a: The timer follows real time, so reopening the tab shows the correct time left. To get the bell while on another tab, allow notifications.

faq.q: Where are the stats stored?
faq.a: In your own browser storage (localStorage), never sent anywhere.

stopwatch.name: Online Stopwatch
stopwatch.desc: A stopwatch accurate to 1/100 second, with laps.
stopwatch.privacy: The stopwatch runs right in your browser; its state is only saved on this device, never sent anywhere.
howto: Click Start or press Space.
Click Lap (L key) to record lap times; the fastest lap is green, the slowest red.
Stop, then click Reset (R key); download the lap table as CSV if needed.

faq.q: Does it keep running if I close the tab or turn off the screen?
faq.a: Yes. Time follows the system clock, so reopening the page shows the right time; the state is saved in your browser.

faq.q: How accurate is it?
faq.a: It displays to 1/100 second. The main error comes from when you press the button (human reaction time is about 0.1–0.2 seconds).

countdown-timer.name: Countdown Timer
countdown-timer.desc: A countdown timer with an alarm and full-screen mode.
countdown-timer.privacy: The timer runs right in your browser; settings are only saved on this device, never sent anywhere.
howto: Quick-pick 1, 3, 5… minutes or enter hours, minutes and seconds.
Click Start (Space key); you can add 1 minute while it runs.
When time's up the alarm rings until you click Mute alarm.

faq.q: Will I hear the alarm on another tab?
faq.a: Yes, unless your device is muted. Click “Enable notifications when on another tab” to also get a system notification.

faq.q: What if my phone's screen locks?
faq.a: Mobile browsers usually pause pages when the screen locks, so the alarm may ring late. While counting, the page keeps the screen on (if the browser supports it).

spin-wheel.name: Spin the Wheel
spin-wheel.desc: Enter a list and spin a random wheel to pick a person, a meal or a prize winner.
spin-wheel.privacy: The list and results are only saved in this device's browser, never sent anywhere.
howto: Enter a list, one item per line (or choose a sample list).
Click Spin, click the wheel or press Space.
Turn on “Remove the winner” for draws with several prizes where each person wins only once.

faq.q: Is the wheel fair?
faq.a: Yes. The result is picked with a secure random generator (crypto.getRandomValues) before the wheel spins; the animation is just for show. Every item has the same chance unless you set weights.

faq.q: How do I make an item more likely to win?
faq.a: Add “* number” after the name, e.g. “Consolation prize * 5” is 5 times as likely as a regular item; its slice on the wheel is bigger too.

faq.q: Is the list saved?
faq.a: Yes, in your device's browser so it's still there next time. Never sent anywhere.

team-picker.name: Random Team Generator
team-picker.desc: Split a list into random teams or draw a random order.
team-picker.privacy: Names are only processed in your browser, never sent anywhere or put in the link.
howto: Enter a list of people, one name per line.
Choose the mode: number of teams, people per team, random order or pick a few people.
Click Draw again if needed, then copy or download the result.

faq.q: Are the teams even?
faq.a: Yes: teams differ by at most 1 person. People in the “Leaders” box are spread one per team first.

faq.q: Is it really random?
faq.a: It uses crypto.getRandomValues and the Fisher–Yates shuffle, so every split is equally likely.

coin-dice.name: Coin Flip & Dice Roller
coin-dice.desc: Flip a coin or roll one or more random dice.
coin-dice.privacy: Results are generated right in your browser with a secure random generator, never sent anywhere.
howto: Choose Flip a coin or Roll dice.
Click the button (or press Space) to flip / roll.
For dice, choose the number of dice (1–10) and sides (4–100); the total shows instantly.

faq.q: Are the results truly random?
faq.a: Yes, they come from the browser's secure random generator with no bias toward any side; the flip animation is just for show.

faq.q: Which side is heads?
faq.a: Heads is the side with the picture, tails the side with the number (denomination).

random-number.name: Random Number Generator
random-number.desc: Generate random numbers in a range, without duplicates, or run a raffle draw.
howto: Enter the range From – To and how many numbers to draw.
Choose no duplicates, sorting, or exclude numbers you don't want.
Turn on “Raffle mode” so drawn numbers don't come up again.

faq.q: Does every number have the same chance?
faq.a: Yes. It uses crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling (no modulo bias), so every number in the range is equally likely.

faq.q: How many numbers can I draw?
faq.a: Up to 10,000 numbers at a time, in a range up to about ±9 quadrillion.

quick-notes.name: Quick Notes
quick-notes.desc: Notes saved right in your browser, auto-saved, downloadable as .txt.
quick-notes.privacy: Notes are stored in this device's own browser (localStorage), never sent anywhere.
howto: Type a note: it's saved automatically on this device.
Click New note to add one; search ignores accents.
Download as .txt, or download all (.zip) as a backup.

faq.q: Where are notes stored?
faq.a: In your device's browser storage (localStorage). Clearing browsing data, using a private window or switching browsers hides them, so download backups.

faq.q: Do notes sync between phone and computer?
faq.a: No, since BbeTools has no server. Several tabs in the same browser stay in sync.

faq.q: How much can I store?
faq.a: A few million characters (the browser limit, usually 5 MB). If it's full, the page tells you to download your notes.

checklist.name: Checklist
checklist.desc: A simple to-do list with drag-and-drop ordering, saved on your device.
checklist.privacy: Lists are stored in this device's own browser (localStorage), never sent anywhere.
howto: Type a task and press Enter (paste several lines to add several tasks at once).
Check off finished tasks; double-click to edit, drag and drop or use ↑↓ to reorder.
Create several lists, use templates, copy or download them as Markdown.

faq.q: Where are lists stored?
faq.a: In your device's browser (localStorage), never sent anywhere. Changing devices or clearing browsing data loses them, so download them if you need to keep them.

faq.q: How do I reuse a list (packing list…)?
faq.a: Click “Uncheck all” to start over without retyping.

world-clock.name: World Clock & Time Zone Converter
world-clock.desc: Current time in cities around the world, and time conversion between time zones.
world-clock.privacy: Times are calculated right in your browser; the city list is only saved on this device.
howto: See the current time in each city; green cells are office hours.
Type a city or country name to add it, click ✕ to remove it.
Turn on “Convert time”, choose a date and time in one city to see the matching times elsewhere (for scheduling online meetings).

faq.q: Is daylight saving time handled?
faq.a: Yes. Browsers include the international time zone database (IANA), so DST is applied correctly for every date, including changeover days.

faq.q: How is the difference shown?
faq.a: Each city shows its UTC offset and how far ahead of or behind your device's time it is.

device-test.name: Camera, Mic, Keyboard & Screen Test
device-test.desc: Test your camera, microphone, left/right speakers, keyboard, mouse and dead pixels on one page before an online meeting.
howto: Choose the device to test: Camera, Microphone, Speakers, Keyboard, Mouse or Screen.
Click Turn camera on / Turn microphone on and allow access when the browser asks.
Follow the instructions in each section: speak, record a 5-second test, press each key, look for dead pixels.

faq.q: Is it safe to let the browser use my camera and mic?
faq.a: Video and audio only show on your device and are never recorded or sent (the 5-second test recording also stays in the browser). Switching sections or closing the page turns the camera and mic off.

faq.q: The camera says it's in use?
faq.a: Close other apps using the camera (Zoom, Teams, Meet in another tab…) and try again.

faq.q: A key doesn't light up?
faq.a: Some keys are handled by the operating system (Fn, Print Screen, volume keys…) so web pages can't receive them; that doesn't mean the key is broken.

webcam-test.name: Webcam Test
webcam-test.desc: Test your webcam or laptop camera online: see the image, resolution, frame rate and take a test photo.
howto: Click Turn camera on and allow the browser to use the camera when asked.
Check that the image is sharp and bright enough; read the resolution and frame rate.
With several cameras, choose another one from the list; click Take a test photo to save a picture.

faq.q: The webcam shows no image, what should I do?
faq.a: Check that the browser is allowed to use the camera (lock icon next to the address bar), close other apps using it (Zoom, Teams…), and see if the laptop has a privacy shutter or camera hotkey. On macOS, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Camera to allow the browser.

faq.q: Why is the image mirrored?
faq.a: The preview is mirrored like a mirror so it's natural to look at; others in a meeting still see it the right way round. You can turn Mirror off.

faq.q: Is the image sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. It only shows on your device; turning the camera off or closing the page stops it.

mic-test.name: Microphone Test
mic-test.desc: Test your microphone online: see the level and waveform as you speak, record 5 seconds and play it back.
howto: Click Turn microphone on and allow the browser to use it when asked.
Say “one, two, three”: the level bar should reach the green zone.
Click Record a 5-second test and play it back to hear how others hear you.

faq.q: The mic picks up nothing?
faq.a: Choose the right microphone in the list (when there are several), check the mute switch on your headset, allow the browser to use the mic (lock icon) and close Zoom/Teams if they're holding it. On macOS, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone.

faq.q: The sound is too quiet or distorted?
faq.a: A level bar in the gray zone is too quiet: move the mic closer or raise the input volume in your sound settings. Hitting the red zone is too loud and may distort.

faq.q: Is the test recording sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. The audio stays in the browser on your device. For longer recordings to download, use the Voice Recorder.

speaker-test.name: Speaker & Headphone Test
speaker-test.desc: Test left and right speakers and headphones; play test tones at many frequencies and a low-to-high sweep.
howto: Start with a low volume.
Click Left speaker, Right speaker and Both to hear the test tone on each side.
Change the frequency or click Sweep from low to high to check for distortion or missing ranges.

faq.q: Left speaker plays on the right?
faq.a: The headphones are worn the wrong way round, the cable is reversed or the balance setting is off. Check your device's sound settings.

faq.q: I can't hear high frequencies?
faq.a: Small speakers and older ears often can't hear sounds above 12,000 Hz; that's normal.

keyboard-test.name: Keyboard Test
keyboard-test.desc: Test your keyboard online: Windows and Mac layouts, laptop or external, with or without a numpad; multi-key rollover and key chatter detection.
keyboard-test.privacy: The keys you press are only processed right in your browser, never recorded or sent anywhere.
howto: Choose the operating system (Windows or Mac), the keyboard type (Laptop or External) and turn on “Has a numeric keypad” if yours has one.
Press each key in turn: received keys turn green; keys that don't change may be dead.
Hold several keys at once to see how many the keyboard registers; chattering keys are highlighted in yellow.

faq.q: A key doesn't light up?
faq.a: Some keys are handled by the operating system (Fn, Print Screen on Windows, volume and brightness keys…) so web pages can't receive them; that doesn't mean the key is broken. Other keys that don't light up may be dead.

faq.q: What is key chatter?
faq.a: One press registers as two (typing “aa” instead of “a”), usually due to a dirty or worn switch. The tool flags any key re-registered within 35 ms of being released.

faq.q: Which layout for a Mac keyboard on Windows (or vice versa)?
faq.a: Choose by the keyboard plugged in. Keys are detected by position, so a Mac keyboard's ⌘ key lights up at the ⌘ spot even on Windows. On a Mac, the F1–F12 row defaults to brightness, volume…: hold fn and press to test.

faq.q: Why hold several keys at once?
faq.a: To see how many keys the keyboard registers at the same time (rollover). Office keyboards often only register 2–6 keys in some combinations; mechanical gaming keyboards usually register all of them (N-key rollover).

mouse-test.name: Mouse Test
mouse-test.desc: Test your mouse online: buttons (including Back/Forward), double-clicks, phantom double-click detection, wheel and polling rate.
mouse-test.privacy: Mouse actions are only processed right in your browser, never recorded or sent anywhere.
howto: Press each mouse button inside the test area: received buttons turn green and are counted.
Click slowly one at a time: if one press registers as two, the tool reports a phantom double-click.
Scroll the wheel and move the mouse quickly inside the area to check the wheel and polling rate.

faq.q: What is a phantom double-click?
faq.a: One press registers as two, usually because the switch inside the mouse is worn. A person needs at least about 80 ms to click twice; the tool warns when two clicks of the same button are under 60 ms apart.

faq.q: What is polling rate?
faq.a: How many times per second the mouse reports its position: office mice are usually 125 Hz, gaming mice 500–1000 Hz or more. Browser measurements are approximate and may be limited by the browser or display.

faq.q: Do Back/Forward buttons navigate away?
faq.a: No, inside the test area these buttons are blocked so you can test freely.

screen-test.name: Dead Pixel Test
screen-test.desc: Find dead pixels, stuck pixels, backlight bleed and uneven colors with full-screen colors; see resolution and refresh rate.
screen-test.privacy: Everything runs right in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.
howto: Clean the screen and click Dead pixel test (full screen).
Click, press → or swipe to cycle through colors: look for dots that stay black or stuck on one color.
On black, check the edges for backlight bleed; on gray, look for blotches; press Esc to exit.

faq.q: What's the difference between dead and stuck pixels?
faq.a: A dead pixel stays black on every background. A stuck pixel stays lit in one color (red, green or blue) whatever the background; stuck pixels sometimes fix themselves.

faq.q: When should I test?
faq.a: Right after buying a new computer or monitor (while you can still return it), and when buying used. Test in a dark room to see backlight bleed clearly.

faq.q: Is the measured refresh rate accurate?
faq.a: Approximately: the page counts how many frames the browser draws per second, which may be lower than the real rate when the device is saving power.

telegram-stickers.name: Telegram Sticker Downloader
telegram-stickers.desc: Download whole Telegram sticker sets: original files (WEBP, TGS, WEBM) or converted to PNG and GIF; also converts .tgs and .webm files you already have.
telegram-stickers.privacy: BbeTools has no server: your browser talks directly to api.telegram.org with your own bot token. .tgs and .webm files you choose are only processed on this device.
howto: In Telegram, open the sticker set → ⋮ → Copy link (like t.me/addstickers/…) and paste it into the Link box.
Paste your bot token (created for free in a minute with @BotFather, see the guide under the box) and click “Get sticker set”.
Choose PNG + GIF or the original format, then click “Download all (.zip)” or click a sticker to download just that one.

faq.q: Does downloading stickers need a server?
faq.a: No. Telegram lets websites call its Bot API directly, so your browser fetches the sticker list and files from api.telegram.org itself. BbeTools has no middleman server and never receives your token or stickers.

faq.q: Why do I need a bot token?
faq.a: Telegram's Bot API only serves sticker files to registered bots. Create a token for free with @BotFather: send /newbot, choose a name, get the token. It's only used in this browser; to cancel it, send /revoke to BotFather.

faq.q: What are TGS and WEBM files?
faq.a: TGS is an animated Lottie sticker (vector, gzip-compressed), WEBM is a video sticker, WEBP is a still image sticker. Choose “PNG + GIF” for files that open everywhere; choose “Original format” to keep full quality for reuse in Telegram.

faq.q: Can't connect to Telegram?
faq.a: Some networks block Telegram, so the browser can't reach api.telegram.org. Try another network. If you saved stickers to your device (Telegram Desktop: right-click → Save), use “From existing files” to convert .tgs and .webm to GIF without any network.

faq.q: Can I use downloaded stickers commercially?
faq.a: Stickers are copyrighted by their creators. Only download them for personal use, or with the creator's permission.

line-stickers.name: LINE Sticker Downloader
line-stickers.desc: Paste a LINE Store link to download a whole LINE sticker or emoji set: original PNG, animated APNG with sound, or converted to GIF. No login needed.
line-stickers.privacy: BbeTools has no server: your browser downloads straight from LINE's server (stickershop.line-scdn.net). No login, and no LINE account details are sent.
howto: Open the sticker or emoji set on store.line.me and copy the page address (or in the LINE app: sticker set page → Share → Copy link).
Paste it into the Link box and click “Get sticker set”; the whole set downloads, including animations and sounds.
Choose PNG + GIF or the original format, then click “Download all (.zip)” or click a sticker to download just that one.

faq.q: Do I need to log in to LINE or buy the set?
faq.a: No login is needed. The page only downloads the image files that the LINE Store shows publicly, for you to save for personal use. To send the stickers in LINE you still need to get or buy the set in LINE.

faq.q: What file format are animated LINE stickers?
faq.a: The originals are animated PNG (APNG), which open in browsers, Telegram, Discord and graphics apps. Choose “PNG + GIF” to convert them to GIF that works everywhere. Stickers with sound also get an .m4a file with the same number.

faq.q: Why do GIF edges look jagged?
faq.a: GIF pixels are either fully transparent or not, so soft sticker edges get rounded off. Pick a White (or Black) background that matches where you'll paste them for smooth edges, or keep the animated PNG (original format).

faq.q: Can I download LINE emoji too?
faq.a: Yes. Paste an emoji set link like store.line.me/emojishop/product/… ; animated emoji are converted to GIF just like stickers.

faq.q: Can I use downloaded stickers commercially?
faq.a: No. Stickers are copyrighted by their creators. Download them for personal use only, or with the creator's permission.

noto-emoji.name: Animated Emoji Downloader
noto-emoji.desc: Search emoji and download Google's animated versions (Noto Animated Emoji) as GIF, WEBP or Lottie, plus large still PNGs.
noto-emoji.privacy: The emoji list ships with BbeTools; emoji images are downloaded by your browser straight from Google Fonts (fonts.gstatic.com). Smaller GIFs are made right on your device.
howto: Type an emoji name (e.g. “smile”, “heart”, “cat”) or paste an emoji into the Search box; you can filter by category.
Click an emoji to see it animated.
Click GIF, WEBP, PNG, SVG or Lottie to download Google's ready-made file, or choose a size and background and click “Make GIF” for a lighter GIF.

faq.q: Where do these animated emoji come from, and can I use them commercially?
faq.a: This is Google's Noto Animated Emoji set, released under the CC BY 4.0 license: you may use it in videos, apps and commercial projects, as long as you give credit (e.g. “Noto Emoji, Google”).

faq.q: Which format should I download?
faq.a: GIF opens everywhere but is heavy with slightly jagged edges; animated WEBP is light with smooth edges, good for the web and chat apps; PNG is a 512 px still image; SVG is a vector that scales without blur; Lottie (JSON) is for developers using lottie-web, lottie-ios or lottie-android.

faq.q: The 512 px GIF is too big?
faq.a: Choose 128 px or 64 px and click “Make GIF”: the page redraws the emoji from its Lottie file into a much lighter GIF, with an optional white or black background for smooth edges.

faq.q: Why are some emoji missing?
faq.a: Google only made animated versions of about 900 popular emoji (smileys, gestures, animals, food…). Emoji not in the list don't have an animated version yet.

signal-stickers.name: Signal Sticker Downloader
signal-stickers.desc: Paste a signal.art/addstickers link to download and decrypt a whole Signal sticker pack right in your browser, as WEBP, PNG or GIF.
signal-stickers.privacy: BbeTools has no server: your browser downloads the encrypted pack from Signal's server (cdn-ca.signal.org) and decrypts it itself. The pack_key is only used on your device and never sent anywhere.
howto: In Signal, open the sticker pack → Share → Copy link (like signal.art/addstickers/#pack_id=…&pack_key=…).
Paste it into the Link box and click “Get sticker pack”; the page downloads and decrypts the whole pack.
Choose PNG + GIF or the original format (WEBP, APNG), then click “Download all (.zip)” or click individual stickers.

faq.q: Why do Signal stickers need decrypting?
faq.a: Signal encrypts every sticker pack on its server (AES-256); only people with the full link have the key (pack_key) to open it. The page uses the key in the link to decrypt right in your browser with Web Crypto, so BbeTools never sees your stickers or key.

faq.q: My link says the key is wrong?
faq.a: The link must include both pack_id (32 characters) and pack_key (64 characters). If you only copied part of it, open the pack in Signal again → Share → Copy link.

faq.q: What format are Signal stickers?
faq.a: Still stickers are usually WEBP; animated ones are animated PNG (APNG) or animated WEBP. Choose “PNG + GIF” for files that open everywhere; choose “Original format” to keep full quality for reuse in Signal, Telegram, WhatsApp.

faq.q: Can I use downloaded stickers commercially?
faq.a: Stickers are copyrighted by their creators. Download them for personal use only, or with the creator's permission.

twitch-emotes.name: Twitch Emote Downloader (7TV, FFZ)
twitch-emotes.desc: Enter a Twitch channel name to view and download its whole 7TV and FrankerFaceZ emote set as a zip: PNG, animated GIF or WEBP, in all 4 sizes.
twitch-emotes.privacy: BbeTools has no server: your browser calls the public APIs of 7TV (7tv.io) and FrankerFaceZ (api.frankerfacez.com) directly and downloads images from their servers. If the channel isn't on FrankerFaceZ, the channel name is sent to api.ivr.fi to look up its ID. No Twitch login needed.
howto: Enter the Twitch channel name (the part after twitch.tv/) or paste a channel link or 7tv.app link, then click “Get emotes”.
Pick a size (4x is the largest) and format: PNG + GIF or the original (WEBP); type a name to filter the emotes you need.
Click “Download all (.zip)” to get the whole set (or the filtered part), or click an emote to download just that one.

faq.q: Which emotes can I download?
faq.a: The 7TV and FrankerFaceZ (FFZ) emotes the channel has added, including animated ones. Native Twitch emotes (subscriber, Bits emotes) aren't available because Twitch only lists them through an API that needs a secret key; BetterTTV emotes can't be downloaded because BetterTTV's image server doesn't let other websites fetch files.

faq.q: PNG + GIF or WEBP?
faq.a: GIF opens everywhere but is larger and has slightly jagged edges. WEBP (7TV's original format) is small with smooth edges and animated emotes keep moving: great for Discord, Telegram and websites. For still emotes PNG and WEBP look the same.

faq.q: How big are 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x?
faq.a: 1x is the Twitch chat size (about 28–32 px), 2x is double, 4x is about 112–128 px. To make Discord emoji (max 128 px) choose 4x. FrankerFaceZ only has 1x, 2x and 4x.

faq.q: My channel shows no emotes?
faq.a: The tool only sees emotes the channel has added on 7TV or FrankerFaceZ. Check the channel name (no spaces). The active 7TV set may change with the season (e.g. a Halloween set); to get another set, paste its 7tv.app/emote-sets/… link.

faq.q: Can I use downloaded emotes commercially?
faq.a: Emotes are copyrighted by their artists or streamers. Download them for personal use only, or with permission.

discord-emoji.name: Discord Emoji & Sticker Downloader
discord-emoji.desc: Paste Discord emoji or sticker links or codes to download the original, largest version (PNG, GIF, WEBP), convert Lottie stickers to GIF, and get whole official sticker packs.
discord-emoji.privacy: BbeTools has no server: your browser downloads straight from Discord's servers (cdn.discordapp.com, media.discordapp.net, discord.com). No login and no Discord token needed.
howto: In Discord (desktop or browser), right-click an emoji or sticker in a message → Copy Link; or type \:emoji_name: to get the code <:name:123…>.
Paste it into the box (several, one per line) and click “Get emoji, stickers”; or choose “Official sticker packs” to get a whole pack from Discord.
Choose PNG + GIF or the original format and a size, then click “Download all (.zip)” or click each one.

faq.q: Can I download all emoji of a server?
faq.a: No. Discord only shows a server's emoji list to logged-in members of that server, so the tool takes emoji one by one from links or codes. You can paste many links at once. Discord's 14 official sticker packs can be downloaded whole.

faq.q: How do I get a Discord emoji link?
faq.a: In Discord on desktop or in a browser: right-click the emoji in a message → Copy Link. Or type a backslash before the emoji (\:name:) and send it; Discord shows a code like <:name:123456…> (or <a:name:…> for animated emoji): paste that code.

faq.q: What size are the downloaded emoji?
faq.a: The original size the creator uploaded to Discord (usually 128 px, sometimes larger), not the small size shown in chat. Pick a smaller size if you need lighter files.

faq.q: What is a Lottie sticker?
faq.a: Most of Discord's official stickers (Wumpus, Clyde…) are Lottie vector animations (.json). Choose “PNG + GIF” and the tool redraws them as GIF right on your device; “Original format” keeps the .json file for developers using lottie-web.

faq.q: Can I use downloaded emoji and stickers commercially?
faq.a: Emoji and stickers are copyrighted by their creators or Discord. Download them for personal use only, or with permission.

youtube-thumbnail.name: YouTube Thumbnail Downloader
youtube-thumbnail.desc: Paste a YouTube video or Shorts link to view and download its thumbnail in every size, up to HD 1280×720; black bars removed automatically, as JPG, PNG or WEBP.
youtube-thumbnail.privacy: BbeTools has no server: your browser downloads images straight from YouTube's image server (i.ytimg.com) and gets the video title via youtube.com/oembed. Format conversion and black-bar removal happen on your device.
howto: Copy a YouTube video link (Share → Copy link); Shorts and youtu.be links work too.
Paste it into the box and click “Get thumbnails”; paste several links, one per line, to get many videos.
Click “Download largest image” or any size; choose JPG, PNG or WEBP and turn on “Remove black bars” if needed.

faq.q: What is the largest thumbnail?
faq.a: HD 1280×720 (maxresdefault). Old videos or videos uploaded in low resolution have no HD version; the tool then uses the largest available size (SD 640×480 or HQ 480×360).

faq.q: Why do SD and HQ images have black bars?
faq.a: YouTube makes SD and HQ images in 4:3, so 16:9 videos get black bars at the top and bottom (Shorts at the sides). Turn on “Remove black bars” to detect and crop them when downloading; for videos without HD, the cropped SD image (640×360) is usually the sharpest.

faq.q: Can I download YouTube videos?
faq.a: No. YouTube doesn't let other websites download videos, and its terms don't allow it. The tool only gets the thumbnail images YouTube makes public.

faq.q: Can I use someone else's thumbnail?
faq.a: Thumbnails are copyrighted by the channel owner. Using them for reference or personal material is fine; to republish or use them commercially you need the owner's permission.
